# Engineer handoff: Colorado eligibility rules for the programs served by PEAK and CBMS

Generated from `volumes/co/`. One line per item. `@assembly` items are implemented in the fact-assembly layer; `@engine` items in the determination engine. Types and scopes are those of the codex. `unknown` propagates: any derivation whose inputs are unknown is unknown unless an `otherwise` supplies a default, and an unknown outcome is reported as *cannot determine* with the list of unknown supplied facts.

Each derivation is given twice: in pattern English, and as the expression tree the ledger stores, which is the form to generate code from. Every operator in the tree is defined in `docs/operators.md` (arguments, unknown propagation, empty groups, numeric and date rules). The same items, trees and parameter versions are available as JSON (`npm run export` writes `conformance/<volume>/ledger.json`), and the conformance suite is `npm run conformance` (`docs/conformance.md`).

## Derived facts

### CO-1356 Has earned income `@engine`

Whether the person has wages or self-employment receipts in the month, the condition on which every program's earned-income verification turns.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program All.
Uses: `self_employment_gross_receipts`, `wages_gross`.

```
any of the following is true:
  - Gross wages is more than 0
  - Self-employment gross receipts is more than 0
```

```json
["any",[">","wages_gross",0],[">","self_employment_gross_receipts",0]]
```

Examples: 3, all passing.

### CO-1357 Has unearned income `@engine`

Whether the person receives Social Security, pension, unemployment, child support, Colorado Works or Adult Financial cash assistance, or other unearned income (taxable, non-taxable or tax-exempt interest) in the month.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program All.
Uses: `adult_financial_cash_income`, `child_support_received`, `other_unearned_income_nontaxable`, `other_unearned_income_taxable`, `pension_income`, `social_security_income`, `tanf_cash_income`, `tax_exempt_interest`, `unemployment_income`.

```
(Social Security income plus Pension income plus Unemployment income plus Child support received plus Colorado Works cash assistance received plus Adult Financial cash assistance received plus Other unearned income, federally taxable plus Other unearned income, not federally taxable plus Tax-exempt interest) is more than 0
```

```json
[">",["+","social_security_income","pension_income","unemployment_income","child_support_received","tanf_cash_income","adult_financial_cash_income","other_unearned_income_taxable","other_unearned_income_nontaxable","tax_exempt_interest"],0]
```

### CO-905 Meets the public assistance citizenship and qualified non-citizen requirement `@engine`

The person is a U.S. citizen or national, or a qualified non-citizen who entered the United States before August 22, 1996, who is in a federal exempt category under 8 U.S.C. 1613(b), or who has held qualified status for five years: the requirement C.R.S. 26-2-111.8(2) sets for Colorado Works, the Old Age Pension, Aid to the Needy Disabled and Aid to the Blind, and that 26-2-706(1.5)(b) and 9 CCR 2503-6 3.604.1.B restate for Colorado Works and 9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.61.C and 3.520.68.A for Aid to the Needy Disabled.

Precision. Vocabulary fix round (R-4, U-2, U-3): the 8 U.S.C. 1613(b) exemption is is_exempt_from_five_year_bar (CO-1725); Colorado Works had read SNAP's own waiting-period exemption, whose under-18 and pre-1931 prongs are not 1613(b) categories (so a lawful permanent resident child inside five years was found eligible and a refugee inside five years was not), and Aid to the Needy Disabled read no exemption at all (so a refugee inside five years failed). The pre-1996 entry test reads us_entry_date (CO-1726), not the date the qualified status was obtained. Once both programs read the same federal exemption, the Colorado Works item and meets_public_assistance_citizenship_requirement (CO-905) were the same rule, as 26-2-111.8(2) makes them; CO-943 is retired into this item, renamed from cw_meets_citizenship_requirement. Adult Financial reads it only for AND and AB (af_category, CO-953): 3.520.61.C and 3.520.68.A state the test 'for AND only', and OAP keeps its own test (af_meets_citizenship_requirement_oap, CO-929). Does not model 26-2-111(2)(c)(II)-(III)'s hardship and SSI-eligibility exceptions (OQ-119).

Type yes/no, scope person, program All.
Uses: `has_held_qualified_status_five_years`, `is_exempt_from_five_year_bar`, `is_qualified_non_citizen`, `is_us_citizen_or_national`, `qualified_non_citizen_entry_cutoff_date`, `us_entry_date`.

```
any of the following is true:
  - Is a U.S. citizen or national
  - all of the following are true:
    - Is a qualified non-citizen
    - any of the following is true:
      - Date of entry into the United States is less than PRWORA qualified-alien entry date cutoff (1996-08-22)
      - Is exempt from the five-year bar (8 U.S.C. 1613(b))
      - Has held qualified status for the five-year waiting period
```

```json
["any","is_us_citizen_or_national",["all","is_qualified_non_citizen",["any",["<","us_entry_date","qualified_non_citizen_entry_cutoff_date"],"is_exempt_from_five_year_bar","has_held_qualified_status_five_years"]]]
```

### CO-1394 SNAP: verification status `@engine`

Where this person's SNAP household stands on verification: not applicable (the person is not a member of a SNAP household); no verification required; complete; complete except that a sponsored non-citizen's sponsor information is outstanding, so that member is ineligible until it is provided and the rest of the household is determined (members excluded, 4.505.7.B); postponed under expedited service (identity verified, other verification outstanding, within the postponement period); pending within the time allowed (ten days from the request, to the thirtieth day after application when only a non-citizen's status document is outstanding, and to the thirtieth day after application when only deductible expenses are); past that time with only deductible expenses unverified (the deductions are disallowed); or past the time allowed with an eligibility factor unverified.

Precision. past_due states only that the time allowed has run with a required factor unverified; when the agency denies (on the thirtieth day, or after a notice of pending status) is application processing and outside this item: 7 CFR 273.2(h)(1)(i)(C) (S813) makes the delay the household's once at least 10 days from the request have passed (OQ-309 resolved). The due date and the household's request date are the evaluated person's.

### CO-1500 SNAP: standard utility allowance `@engine`

The one standard utility allowance Colorado's four-tiered mandatory SUA gives the person's SNAP household - the Heating and Cooling Utility Allowance when the household is entitled to it; otherwise the Basic Utility Allowance for at least two non-heating, non-cooling utility costs; otherwise the One Utility Allowance for one such cost other than a telephone; otherwise the telephone allowance when the telephone is the only utility cost; otherwise nothing - per 10 CCR 2506-1 4.407.31. A household receives only one of the four allowances and cannot claim actual utility expenses. Internet connection fees never enter it (4.407.3.E.5; Pub. L. 119-21 sec. 10104).

Precision. Household-level: the utility facts (snap_entitled_to_heating_cooling_allowance, non_heating_utility_cost_count, incurs_telephone_cost) are household facts stated on one member, usually the head; the allowance is the highest tier any member of snap_household_members states, so stating the same utilities on two members still gives one allowance (4.407.31, 'only entitled to one (1) of the four (4) utility allowances'). A member whose facts are unstated contributes nothing (P4 defaults of false and zero, the same device OQ-29 records for shelter costs); a household where no member states them gets no allowance. Every member of the household evaluates to the same figure, which snap_shelter_costs (CO-377) adds once. A case may still state this amount directly on a person, which the engine uses for that person in place of the rule. A household sharing utility costs with another SNAP household receives the full allowance (4.407.31.A.1.d, B.2, C.2, D.1), which needs no separate term.

Type money, scope person, program SNAP.
Uses: `incurs_telephone_cost`, `non_heating_utility_cost_count`, `snap_entitled_to_heating_cooling_allowance`, `snap_household_members`, `snap_sua_basic`, `snap_sua_heating_cooling`, `snap_sua_one_utility`, `snap_sua_telephone`.

```
if there is a person in SNAP: household members such that
    that person's SNAP: entitled to the heating and cooling utility allowance, otherwise no
  then SNAP heating and cooling standard utility allowance (616)
else if there is a person in SNAP: household members such that
    (that person's Number of non-heating utility costs incurred, otherwise 0) is at least 2
  then SNAP basic utility allowance (390)
else if there is a person in SNAP: household members such that
    all of the following are true:
      - (that person's Number of non-heating utility costs incurred, otherwise 0) is equal to 1
      - it is not the case that that person's Incurs a telephone cost
  then SNAP one utility allowance (73)
else if there is a person in SNAP: household members such that
    (that person's Number of non-heating utility costs incurred, otherwise 0) is equal to 1
  then SNAP telephone allowance (100)
otherwise 0
```

### CO-2003 SNAP: child support exclusion `@engine`

The legally obligated child support the person pays that SNAP excludes from the person's gross income for the month: with a history of three or more months of payments, the average of the payments in the three months before the month; otherwise the month's anticipated payment, which is the estimate 4.407.5.E calls for.

Precision. The average is taken over the three months before the budget month (P17). 4.407.5.D also adjusts the average for "any anticipated changes in the legal obligation"; a case with such a change states the changed figure as the month's payment and a history shorter than three months, or states the prior months as the adjusted figures. A payment history with no stated length is read as none (snap_child_support_payment_history_months, CO-2002), so the month's payment is used, as before.

Type money, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `child_support_paid_legally_obligated`, `snap_child_support_payment_history_months`.

```
if (SNAP: months of child support payment history, otherwise 0) is at least 3
  then Child support paid, legally obligated averaged over the 3 consecutive months ending with the month before the month
otherwise Child support paid, legally obligated
```

### CO-2300 SNAP: counted shelter cost of a member `@engine`

The part of the shelter costs billed to or paid by this household member (shelter_cost_monthly) that counts as a shelter cost of the household: all of it for an eligible member and for a member disqualified for IPV or fraud, a work-requirement sanction (a voluntary quit included) or as a fleeing felon or probation or parole violator; for a member disqualified as an ineligible non-citizen, the cost divided evenly among every household member, the disqualified member included, less the disqualified member's own share; nothing for an ineligible student, who is not a household member, or for any other ineligible member.

Precision. n is the count of snap_household_members, the disqualified member included, as in snap_counted_income_of_ineligible_member (CO-333). Each disqualified member's cost loses that member's one share, the reading CO-333 gives the income of 4.411.1.B.2.b. The standard utility allowance is not prorated (4.411.1.B.2.c); snap_shelter_costs (CO-377) adds it once in full. A drug-felony disqualification counts nothing, matching CO-333, which counts none of that member's income. Unknown when this member's shelter_cost_monthly is unstated.

Type money, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `shelter_cost_monthly`, `snap_household_members`, `snap_is_disqualified_member_counted_in_full`, `snap_is_ineligible_member`, `snap_is_ineligible_non_citizen`.

```
if it is not the case that SNAP: is an ineligible member
  then Shelter cost, monthly
else if SNAP: is a disqualified member whose income and expenses count in full
  then Shelter cost, monthly
else if SNAP: is an ineligible non-citizen
  then Shelter cost, monthly times (((the number of persons in SNAP: household members) minus 1) divided by (the number of persons in SNAP: household members))
otherwise 0
```

The part of the dependent care expense billed to or paid by this household member (dependent_care_expense) that counts toward the household's dependent care deduction: all of it for an eligible member and for a member disqualified for IPV or fraud, a work-requirement sanction (a voluntary quit included) or as a fleeing felon or probation or parole violator; for a member disqualified as an ineligible non-citizen, the expense divided equally among every household member, the disqualified member included, less the disqualified member's own share; nothing for an ineligible student or any other ineligible member.

Precision. Same arms and the same n as snap_counted_shelter_cost_of_member (CO-2300). Unknown when this member's dependent_care_expense is unstated.

Type money, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `dependent_care_expense`, `snap_household_members`, `snap_is_disqualified_member_counted_in_full`, `snap_is_ineligible_member`, `snap_is_ineligible_non_citizen`.

```
if it is not the case that SNAP: is an ineligible member
  then Dependent care expense
else if SNAP: is a disqualified member whose income and expenses count in full
  then Dependent care expense
else if SNAP: is an ineligible non-citizen
  then Dependent care expense times (((the number of persons in SNAP: household members) minus 1) divided by (the number of persons in SNAP: household members))
otherwise 0
```

### CO-2305 SNAP: is the initial month `@engine`

The month is the household's initial month of application: the month containing the date of application, when the determination is not a recertification applied for before the certification period expired (10 CCR 2506-1 4.000.1 "Initial month of application") and the household is not a migrant or seasonal farmworker household in the job stream with a break in participation of thirty days or less (4.207.2.B).

### CO-2307 SNAP: full month allotment `@engine`

This person's SNAP household's allotment for a full month - the maximum allotment less the benefit reduction, rounded down to the nearest dollar (10 CCR 2506-1 4.207.3.A.3) and floored at $0, with a one- or two-person household that meets the net income test receiving at least the minimum allotment (4.207.3.C) - the benefit for every month except an initial month, and the full month's benefit an initial month is prorated from.

Precision. The minimum allotment floor applies only to a household of snap_minimum_allotment_household_size_limit (2) or fewer eligible members that passes every applicable eligibility test - the gross income test, the net income test, and the resource test - not the net income test alone; a household that fails any of those tests is not "eligible" within the meaning of S104's "all eligible one-person and two-person households" and gets $0, not the floor. A three-or-more-member household whose maximum-allotment-less-reduction is $0 (or negative, already floored at $0) simply receives $0; whether that household is denied depends on categorical eligibility (snap_eligibility_status, CO-387; OQ-26 resolved). Rounding down is written as the negated ceiling of the negated difference, the shape the volume uses for a floor.

Type money, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `snap_benefit_reduction`, `snap_eligible_household_size`, `snap_maximum_allotment`, `snap_meets_gross_income_test`, `snap_meets_net_income_test`, `snap_meets_resource_limit`, `snap_minimum_allotment`, `snap_minimum_allotment_household_size_limit`.

```
if it is not the case that (all of the following are true:;   - SNAP: meets the gross income test;   - SNAP: meets the net income test;   - SNAP: meets the resource limit)
  then 0
else if all of the following are true:
    - SNAP: number of eligible household members is at most SNAP minimum allotment household size limit (2)
    - SNAP: meets the net income test
  then the greater of the greater of 0 and 0 minus (SNAP: benefit reduction minus SNAP: maximum allotment rounded up to the next whole dollar) and SNAP minimum allotment (25)
otherwise the greater of 0 and 0 minus (SNAP: benefit reduction minus SNAP: maximum allotment rounded up to the next whole dollar)
```

```json
["case",[["not",["all","snap_meets_gross_income_test","snap_meets_net_income_test","snap_meets_resource_limit"]],0],[["all",["<=","snap_eligible_household_size","snap_minimum_allotment_household_size_limit"],"snap_meets_net_income_test"],["max",["max",0,["-",0,["ceil",["-","snap_benefit_reduction","snap_maximum_allotment"]]]],"snap_minimum_allotment"]],["else",["max",0,["-",0,["ceil",["-","snap_benefit_reduction","snap_maximum_allotment"]]]]]]
```

### CO-2308 SNAP: prorated initial month allotment `@engine`

The household's benefit for its initial month before the minimum-allotment test: the full month's benefit computed without the one- and two-person minimum (which applies "Except for an initial month", 4.207.3.C), times the number of days from the date of application through the end of the month, divided by the number of days in the month, rounded down to the lower whole dollar; $0 when the household fails the gross income, net income or resource test.

Precision. Days from the application date to the first day of the next month equal 4.207.2.C's "Number of days in month plus one" less "the date of application". 4.207.2.C does not state the rounding; 7 CFR 273.10(a)(1)(iii)(C) rounds the product down, and the floor is written as the negated ceiling of the negated value.


### CO-2337 SNAP: sponsor deeming applies `@engine`

The sponsor's (and sponsor's spouse's) income and resources are deemed to this person for SNAP: the person is a sponsored non-citizen (an affidavit of support executed on or after December 19, 1997, is_sponsored_non_citizen) who is not a member of the sponsor's SNAP household, is not sponsored by an organization, is not indigent, is not exempt as a battered non-citizen, whose sponsor has not died, and who has not worked or been credited with forty quarters under Title II (10 CCR 2506-1 4.305.2.A, E).

Precision. A non-citizen who needs no sponsor (a refugee, parolee, asylee or Cuban or Haitian entrant, E.3) or who has naturalized (E.6) has no affidavit of support in force and states is_sponsored_non_citizen false. The forty quarters are qualifying_quarters, which already includes quarters credited from a spouse or parent, against snap_qualifying_quarters_threshold (CO-103). Only an eligible sponsored non-citizen has the sponsor's income deemed (4.305.2.C); snap_requires_verification_of_sponsor (CO-1616) reads this item for a household member.

Type yes/no, scope person, program SNAP.
Uses: `is_sponsored_non_citizen`, `qualifying_quarters`, `snap_battered_non_citizen_sponsor_exemption_applies`, `snap_is_indigent_non_citizen`, `snap_lives_in_sponsor_household`, `snap_qualifying_quarters_threshold`, `sponsor_has_died`, `sponsor_is_organization`.

```
  - it is not the case that Sponsor is an organization, otherwise no
  - it is not the case that SNAP: is an indigent non-citizen, otherwise no
  - it is not the case that SNAP: battered non-citizen exemption from sponsor deeming applies, otherwise no
  - it is not the case that Sponsor has died, otherwise no
  - Qualifying quarters is less than SNAP non-citizen qualifying-quarters threshold (40)
```

### CO-305 SNAP: household members `@engine`

The persons who make up this person's SNAP purchase-and-prepare unit under 7 CFR 273.1(a)-(b)(1) and 10 CCR 2506-1 4.304 - everyone reachable from this person by a chain of buys_prepares_with, spouse, mandatory-member parent/child, or mandatory-member caretaker/dependent edges, minus anyone excluded as an institution resident. A buys_prepares_with edge is not crossed into or out of a household of an elderly person with a disability and that person's spouse granted separate household status under 7 CFR 273.1(b)(2) (snap_is_in_elderly_disabled_separate_household, CO-2304). Each member's value of this item is the same set (their own unit); a person who is not a household member (an institution resident) has no unit, so the value is empty for them.

Precision. A parent/child edge is only crossed into the household when the child member of that pair is under snap_mandatory_child_age (22), matching the "person under 22 ... living with parent" mandatory-combination rule (7 CFR 273.1(b)(1)(ii); 10 CCR 2506-1 4.304.1.A.1). A caretaker/dependent edge is only crossed when the dependent is under snap_parental_control_age (18) and is_under_parental_control_of_household_member is true for the dependent, matching the separate "child... under 18... under the parental control of a household member other than his or her parent" mandatory combination (7 CFR 273.1(b)(1)(iii); 10 CCR 2506-1 4.304.1.A.2). A spouse edge always crosses, matching 273.1(b)(1)(i); a buys_prepares_with edge crosses (273.1(a)(3)) unless either end is in a separate elderly and disabled household (273.1(b)(2), 4.304.3.A; phase-10 sweep, OQ-37). The mandatory parent/child and caretaker edges still cross, since 4.304.1 keeps mandatory members together.

Type group of persons, scope person, program SNAP.
Uses: `age`, `is_under_parental_control_of_household_member`, `relationships`, `snap_is_household_member`, `snap_is_in_elderly_disabled_separate_household`, `snap_mandatory_child_age`, `snap_parental_control_age`.

### CO-306 SNAP: is exempt from the non-citizen waiting period `@engine`

A qualified non-citizen subject to the additional condition (10 CCR 2506-1 4.305,B,3) is exempt from the five-year/40-quarter waiting period because they are under 18, are blind or a person with a disability and receive benefits or assistance for that condition (whatever their entry date), have a military connection, or were born on or before August 22, 1931 and obtained their qualifying status on or before August 22, 1996.

Precision. The "born on or before August 22, 1931 and lawfully resided in the U.S. on August 22, 1996" test (S15) is modeled as date_of_birth on or before 1931-08-22 and qualified_status_date on or before 1996-08-22 (qualified_status_date stands in for lawful residence on that date, a fact this volume does not separately collect). The blind or disabled exception (4.305.B.3.d, S1305; 8 U.S.C. 1612(a)(2)(F)(ii), S1306) reads snap_is_disabled_member (CO-302): "receiving benefits or assistance for blindness or disability" within the meaning of 7 U.S.C. 2012 is the benefit-receipt list of the 7 CFR 271.2 elderly-or-disabled definition, and it has no August 22, 1996 condition (OQ-2 resolved: the brief had merged this exception with the elderly one).

Type yes/no, scope person, program SNAP.
Uses: `age`, `date_of_birth`, `has_military_connection`, `qualified_status_date`, `snap_immigrant_child_exemption_age`, `snap_is_disabled_member`.

```
any of the following is true:
  - Age is less than SNAP immigrant child exemption age (18)
  - SNAP: is a disabled member
  - Has a military connection
  - all of the following are true:
    - Date of birth is at most 1931-08-22
    - Qualified status date is at most 1996-08-22
```

Precision. The pro rata share divides the member's income evenly among every household member counted by snap_household_members (including the ineligible member), then counts all but that one share; n is the count of that person's whole purchase-and-prepare unit, not just the eligible members.

```
otherwise 0
```

### CO-417 SNAP: countable ABAWD months in the current 36-month clock period `@engine`

The number of countable ABAWD months accrued in Colorado's current fixed 36-month clock period before the month in context - from the most recent reset (July 2023, July 2026, July 2029, ...) through the month before - since the clock 'resets accrued countable months and ABAWD disqualifications, regardless of start date, for all ABAWDs every thirty-six (36) calendar months starting July 1, 2023' (10 CCR 2506-1 4.311.3.C.2).

Precision. Evaluated per month, not only as of the determination date. The period start is the clock start month plus 36 times the whole number of 36-month periods elapsed (whole years between the first days of the two months, divided by three and rounded down; floor(x) is computed as -ceil(-x)). In the reset month itself nothing has accrued yet. A month before July 2023 keeps the rolling 36-month count 7 CFR 273.24(b)(3) also allows. Phase-8 fix round (K-6): the item counted a rolling 36 months, which is not the clock Colorado chose.

Type whole number, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `snap_abawd_clock_start_month`, `snap_abawd_countable_month`, `snap_abawd_period_months`.

```
  then the number of months in the SNAP ABAWD time limit period, months (36) consecutive months ending with the month before the month for which SNAP: is a countable ABAWD month for the month
otherwise the number of months in the months from SNAP ABAWD time limit period, months (36) times (-1 times (-1 times ((the number of whole years between the first day of SNAP ABAWD time limit clock start month (2023-07) and the first day of the month) divided by (SNAP ABAWD time limit period, months (36) divided by 12)) rounded up to the next whole dollar)) months after SNAP ABAWD time limit clock start month (2023-07) through the month before the month for which SNAP: is a countable ABAWD month for the month
```

Not subject when the person is outside the ABAWD age range or otherwise exempt from the time limit for the month; within limit when countable months in the current 36-month clock period are below the 3-month limit; regained when the person has reached the limit but regained eligibility (4.311.3.D.1) and meets the work requirement in the month (D.2); additional months when the person, having regained eligibility, is in the single three-month period after notifying the office of no longer meeting it (D.3); otherwise limit reached.

Precision. Regained eligibility and the additional months come from snap_abawd_eligibility_regained (CO-2309) and snap_abawd_is_in_additional_months (CO-2312), both read as false when not stated; a person who becomes exempt is not subject (D.1.d).

### CO-419 SNAP: meets the elderly/disabled separate-household election `@engine`

An otherwise eligible member who is sixty or older and unable to purchase and prepare their own meals because of a permanent disability may elect, with their spouse, to be a SNAP household separate from the others they live with, unless the income of those others (excluding the elderly/disabled member and their spouse) exceeds 165 percent of the federal poverty line for the size of that "others" group.

Precision. The 'others' group is this person's physical residence-sharing group (everyone reachable by a chain of buys_prepares_with or spouse edges), minus this person and this person's spouse (if any); their combined snap_person_gross_income for the month, compared against snap_elderly_disabled_separate_household_income_limit_table (CO-114) keyed by the others' count (floored at 1, since the table has no size-0 entry). The person must ask for the separate household (snap_requests_elderly_disabled_separate_household, CO-2303, read as false when unstated) and be sixty or older (snap_is_elderly; 273.1(b)(2) and 4.304.3.A both say sixty or older). Phase-10 sweep (OQ-37): snap_household_members (CO-305) now reads this item through snap_is_in_elderly_disabled_separate_household (CO-2304); because the others are the physical residence group, not the composed household, there is no cycle. Colorado's 4.304.3.A.2 counts the spouse in the others' household when the spouse is the one purchasing and preparing meals; no fact says who purchases and prepares, so the spouse is always set aside, as 273.1(b)(2) states.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program SNAP.

### CO-1150 Medicaid: meets every requirement other than citizenship or immigration status `@engine`

Whether the person is a Colorado resident who meets the criteria of one of the categorical Medical Assistance programs apart from citizenship and immigration status - not excluded as a patient in an institution for mental diseases (§ 8.100.3.G.1.c), and a MAGI category (whose income test is part of the category), the SSI-related aged, blind or disabled income and resource standards, OAP SISC B (an aged, blind or disabled OAP recipient within the SSI resource standard, § 8.100.6.K.4), or institutional long-term care financial eligibility with the nursing facility level of care - the "otherwise meets the eligibility requirements" condition of 42 U.S.C. 1396b(v)(2)(B), 42 CFR 440.255(c)(2) and 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.3.F.1.k.

Precision. The routes are the categorical programs this volume derives without reading citizenship: ma_magi_category (CO-551), the SSI-related financial tests (CO-603, CO-609, CO-610; ma_is_ssi_related_eligible itself reads citizenship and so cannot be used), OAP SISC B without its status term (af_category, CO-953, with CO-603 and CO-610; ma_oap_sisc_b_eligible, CO-1177, reads status), and the institutional long-term care tests (CO-640, CO-651). The non-MAGI routes require the person to be aged, blind or disabled, as §§ 8.100.3.F.1.b-d and f-g state, so a person who is not is settled without the long-term care facts. The Buy-In programs, HCBS waivers and PACE are not routes: their own items read status (CO-618, CO-620 through CO-1174; CO-653 and CO-654 since the phase 7 fix round, B-3), and an HCBS or PACE applicant who fails status is emergency-eligible here only through the SSI-related or OAP route (OQ-200). 1396b(v)(2)(B) excludes the requirement of receiving SSI or a State supplementary payment, which the SSI-related route does not test.

### CO-1151 Medicaid: emergency Medicaid status `@engine`

The emergency Medicaid determination for the month. A Colorado resident who meets the citizenship and immigration status requirement (CO-509), or a child, pregnant or postpartum person who is fully covered under Cover All Coloradans in a category § 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.1.a-b lists (CO-1175) or eligible for CHP+ under 10 CCR 2505-3 § 110.1.B.5.o, is not limited to emergency coverage (not_applicable_status_met). A resident who fails status but meets every other requirement of a categorical program is limited to emergency (and reproductive) services (10 CCR 2505-10 §§ 8.100.3.F.1.k, 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.2; 42 U.S.C. 1396b(v); 42 CFR 435.406(b), 435.350, 440.255(c)); the coverage pays for this month's care when the person has an emergency medical condition (eligible_emergency_condition) and otherwise stands without a covered service (eligible_no_current_emergency). ineligible_residency and ineligible_other_requirements report the failing condition.

Precision. Residency first, then status, then the other requirements (ma_is_emergency_medicaid_only, CO-510, which reads ma_meets_requirements_other_than_status, CO-1150), then the month's emergency medical condition. Colorado's emergency eligibility does not wait for an emergency: the application is complete without a physician statement and an approved member is not asked to reapply for 12 months (§ 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.2), so eligible_no_current_emergency is an eligible member with nothing to pay for this month, not a denial. Prenatal care and follow-up care are outside emergency-only coverage (§ 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.2); a pregnant person regardless of status is instead covered through MAGI Pregnant or CHP+ prenatal under Cover All Coloradans (§ 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.1; 10 CCR 2505-3 § 110.1.B.5.o), so reaches not_applicable_status_met here when either covers her. Phase 7 fix round: a lawfully present adult who is not pregnant (Temporary Protected Status, for example) no longer meets status (B-1), so is emergency-only when otherwise eligible; a child, pregnant or postpartum person meets status here only when covered in a listed category or by CHP+, so an undocumented postpartum adult whose only category is Adult is emergency-only (S-2); and long-term care now tests status (B-3), so an undocumented nursing facility resident is ineligible_status there and emergency-eligible here, not both eligible. The fetched 10 CCR 2505-3 states no separate unborn-child (from-conception) CHIP category.

Type one of, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `chp_eligibility_status`, `has_emergency_medical_condition`, `ma_is_cover_all_coloradans_person`, `ma_is_covered_under_cover_all_coloradans`, `ma_is_emergency_medicaid_only`, `ma_meets_citizenship_requirement`, `ma_meets_residency`.

```
if it is not the case that Medicaid: meets the residency requirement
  then ineligible_residency
else if any of the following is true:
    - Medicaid: meets the citizenship requirement
    - Medicaid: is covered under Cover All Coloradans
    - all of the following are true:
      - Medicaid: is a Cover All Coloradans person
      - CHP+: eligibility status is one of: eligible_child, eligible_prenatal
  then not_applicable_status_met
else if it is not the case that Medicaid: is emergency Medicaid only
  then ineligible_other_requirements
else if Has an emergency medical condition
  then eligible_emergency_condition
otherwise eligible_no_current_emergency
```

Status reads ma_meets_status_for_cover_all_coloradans_categories (CO-1174): the citizen and qualified non-citizen categories § 8.715.2.C.3 names (ma_meets_citizenship_requirement, CO-509, which also covers § 8.100.3.G.1.g.v's Cuban/Haitian entrants and COFA migrants that C.3's '(ii)-(iv)' skips) and the exception C.3 cross-references as '8.100.3(G)(1)(g)(viii)', read as the Cover All Coloradans exception now numbered ix (OQ-202). ### CO-1154 Medicaid: family planning and reproductive health care status `@engine`

Which route, if any, gives the person family planning services this month. A person eligible for a Medicaid category that provides full coverage (ma_has_full_coverage_category, CO-1176) or for the Breast and Cervical Cancer Program (whose clients receive all State Plan benefits, § 8.715.7.A) gets family planning services as a Medicaid client (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.730.2.A), as does a child under 19 eligible for state medical assistance (C.R.S. 25.5-2-104(2)) - full_coverage. A resident who meets the citizenship and immigration status requirement, is not fully covered, and whose family planning household income is over 133% and within 260% FPL qualifies for Limited Family Planning Medical Assistance (§ 8.100.4.G.8) - limited_family_planning. A resident with reproductive capacity who would be eligible for Medical Assistance but for immigration status qualifies for the state-only reproductive health-care program (C.R.S. 25.5-2-103; § 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.2's reproductive care regardless of status) - reproductive_health_care_program.

Precision. Order: residency; full coverage; for a person meeting status (CO-509), the income band (otherwise ineligible_income); for a person failing status, reproductive capacity and eligibility but for status (otherwise ineligible). Limited family planning is not among the categories Cover All Coloradans reaches (§ 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.1.a-b) and § 8.100.4.G.8 requires 'immigration or citizenship status', so the status test is CO-509 alone and an undocumented pregnant woman who is not fully covered reaches the reproductive health-care program (phase 7 fix round, S-2; OQ-214). 'Would be eligible to enroll in the medical assistance program ... but is not eligible due solely to the individual's immigration status' (25.5-2-103(1)(b)) is read as meeting a categorical program other than status (ma_is_emergency_medicaid_only, CO-510) or the Limited Family Planning income band (OQ-205). A child under 19 who fails status and meets either is eligible for state medical assistance (C.R.S. 25.5-2-104(2)), which includes all Medical Assistance benefits, and so is reported full_coverage, not the reproductive health-care program, which 25.5-2-103(1)(b) closes to a person eligible for state medical assistance; a child who has declined state medical assistance (ma_has_declined_state_medical_assistance, CO-2207; OQ-205, resolved) is not reported full_coverage, and reaches the reproductive health-care program when the child has reproductive capacity. Limited family planning is read by the letter of § 8.100.4.G.8 ('no age or gender restriction'), although § 8.730.1 defines family planning services as services to individuals of child-bearing age (OQ-215). Phase 7 fix round (S-1): full coverage reads the shared union CO-1176, which adds the protected groups and OAP SISC B, and BCCP is added here.

Type one of, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `age`, `has_reproductive_capacity`, `ma_bccp_eligibility_status`, `ma_family_planning_income_in_band`, `ma_has_declined_state_medical_assistance`, `ma_has_full_coverage_category`, `ma_is_emergency_medicaid_only`, `ma_magi_child_age_limit`, `ma_meets_citizenship_requirement`, `ma_meets_residency`.

```
  then ineligible_residency
else if any of the following is true:
    - Medicaid: has a full-coverage Medicaid category
```

### CO-1156 Medicaid: Old Age Pension Health Care Program status `@engine`

Whether an Old Age Pension recipient gets medical care through the state-only Old Age Pension Health Care Program (SISC C). The program serves persons receiving OAP-A or OAP-B who do not qualify for Medicaid (10 CCR 2505-10 §§ 8.941.1, 8.941.1.A, 8.941.3; § 8.100.3.F.1.j; § 8.100.6.K.7) and who are not patients in an institution for tuberculosis or behavioral or mental health disorders (C.R.S. 25.5-2-101(2)). An OAP recipient who receives SSI or meets SSI eligibility criteria, even except for income, is Medicaid-eligible instead (SISC B, § 8.100.6.K.2-4).

Precision. OAP receipt reads af_category (CO-953) as oap (9 CCR 2503-5 now states a single OAP category; OAP-A/OAP-B survive only as the Medicaid labels of 8.100.6.K.1, OQ-111); AND-CS, AND-SO and AB recipients are not OAP recipients (§ 8.941.3.B). 'Meets SSI eligibility criteria except for the level of their income' (§ 8.100.6.K.4) is ma_oap_sisc_b_eligible (CO-1177, phase 7 fix round S-3): residency, Medicaid's citizenship and immigration requirement (CO-509), aged, blind or disabled (CO-603) and within the SSI resource standard (CO-610) - OAP itself has no five-year bar (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.67.E, af_meets_citizenship_requirement_oap, CO-929), so a qualified non-citizen inside the bar can receive OAP but not SSI-related Medicaid, which is the population SISC C serves; full MAGI eligibility (CO-562) also counts as qualifying for Medicaid. OAP-C (court-committed) recipients are excluded by § 8.941.3.B; af_category has no OAP-C option, so receipt is the supplied receives_oap_c (CO-2208) and such a recipient who does not qualify for Medicaid is reported ineligible_oap_c (OQ-206, resolved). Eligibility is not retroactive (§ 8.941.1.E); this item states the month's status. § 8.100.6.K.7's OAP-A, OAP-B and OAP Refugee recipients who lost OAP to a cost of living adjustment other than OASDI remain in SISC C: ma_lost_oap_to_non_oasdi_cost_of_living_adjustment (CO-2209) brings them in as if they still received OAP (OQ-206, resolved); a current OAP Refugee recipient is an OAP recipient in af_category. Vocabulary fix round (docs/reviews/vocabulary-reuse.md, R-14): the institutional exclusion reads ma_oap_is_patient_in_tb_or_mental_health_institution (CO-1748).

### CO-1158 Medicaid: Pickle countable income `@engine`

The person's SSI-related countable income after the Pickle disregard - the cumulative OASDI increases since SSI or OAP was lost (current OASDI less the OASDI that caused the loss) are subtracted (10 CCR 2505-10 §§ 8.100.6.D.1, 8.100.6.E.1.d-e).

Precision. OQ-207 resolved: the Pickle disregard comes off the OASDI benefit first (42 CFR 435.135(a)(3): deducted from current OASDI benefits; § 8.100.6.E.1.e: subtract the disregard from the current OASDI income to get the countable OASDI income), and the SSI exclusions then apply to the reduced income: the household's unearned income less the disregard, less the $20 general exclusion, with any unused part of the $20 and the $65 earned exclusion and one-half disregard applied to earned income as in ma_ssi_countable_earned_income (CO-605). ### CO-1172 Medicaid: is exempt from the five-year rule `@engine`

Whether a qualified non-citizen is exempt from Medical Assistance's five-year rule under 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.3.G.1.g.iv-v: a refugee, asylee, Cuban or Haitian entrant or Compact of Free Association migrant (iv.9-10, v.1-2, "on any date"); an honorably discharged veteran or a person on active duty, or the spouse or dependent child of one (iv.2-3); a Lawful Permanent Resident who has worked 40 work quarters (iv.1); or a person in one of the other iv categories (iv.4-8, 11, and a refugee or asylee who has adjusted to LPR, iv.9-10).

Precision. Refugees and asylees are exempt whether or not they have adjusted to LPR: § 8.100.3.G.1.g.iv opens with "Be a Legal Permanent Resident" but lists persons "granted asylum" and "refugee" (iv.9-10) and trafficking victims (iv.11), and 8 U.S.C. 1613(b)(1), which iv cites, exempts refugees and asylees as such; reading iv as excluding an unadjusted refugee would leave refugees and asylees under no adult category at all (OQ-213). The 40-quarters exemption is read for a Lawful Permanent Resident only, as iv states it; qualifying_quarters (CO-004) counts quarters credited from a parent's or spouse's work as 8 U.S.C. 1612(b)(2)(B), which iv.1 cites, allows. The veteran and active-duty exemption is read for any qualified non-citizen, as the item it replaces did. This item does not itself test that the person is a qualified non-citizen; ma_meets_citizenship_requirement (CO-509) reads it only for one. Vocabulary fix round (R-4): the 8 U.S.C. 1613(b) categories (refugee, asylee, Cuban or Haitian entrant, COFA migrant, veteran or active duty, and a refugee or asylee adjusted to LPR or an Amerasian immigrant) are read from the shared is_exempt_from_five_year_bar (CO-1725), so Medicaid and the cash programs cannot disagree on them; ma_five_year_bar_exempt_category (CO-1170) now carries only the categories of iv that 1613(b) does not list.

Type yes/no, scope person, program Medicaid.
Uses: `citizenship_status`, `is_exempt_from_five_year_bar`, `ma_five_year_bar_exempt_category`, `ma_five_year_bar_exempt_work_quarters`, `qualifying_quarters`.

```
any of the following is true:
  - Is exempt from the five-year bar (8 U.S.C. 1613(b))
  - it is not the case that Medicaid: five-year-rule exempt immigrant category is equal to none
  - all of the following are true:
    - Citizenship status is equal to lawful_permanent_resident
    - Qualifying quarters is at least Medicaid: work quarters that exempt a Lawful Permanent Resident from the five-year rule (40)
```

### CO-1175 Medicaid: is covered under Cover All Coloradans `@engine`

Whether a person who does not meet the citizenship and immigration status requirement (ma_meets_citizenship_requirement, CO-509) is nevertheless fully covered this month through Cover All Coloradans (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.1): a child, pregnant or postpartum person (ma_is_cover_all_coloradans_person, CO-1173) who qualifies for a Medical Assistance category ix.1.a-b lists - the MAGI Children or Pregnant category (including a needy newborn), a Buy-In program, or an HCBS waiver.

Precision. The MAGI categories are read from ma_magi_category (CO-551), which does not read status; needy_newborn is counted with child, since a needy newborn is a child under 19 in the Children's group. Transitional Medical Assistance, the 4 Month Extended Medical Assistance and Psych <21 are not modeled in this volume. CHP+ is not a Medical Assistance category; ma_emergency_medicaid_status (CO-1151) reads CHP+ eligibility separately. OQ-214 sweep: a child under 19 or a pregnant person who meets every requirement of any categorical program other than status (ma_meets_requirements_other_than_status, CO-1150) is covered here too, by C.R.S. 25.5-2-104(2) (state medical assistance for a child, the same benefits) and 25.5-5-201(6)(a) (medical assistance for a pregnant non-citizen); a postpartum person who was not covered while pregnant still reaches only the ix.1.a-b list. ### CO-1177 Medicaid: is eligible as an OAP recipient meeting SSI criteria except income (SISC B) `@engine`

Whether the person is an Old Age Pension recipient who receives Medical Assistance under SISC B because the person also meets SSI eligibility criteria except for the level of income - 10 CCR 2505-10 §§ 8.100.6.K.2-4, 8.100.3.F.1.c-d and 8.100.3.M.2.b: receives OAP (af_category, CO-953), a Colorado resident, meets Medicaid's citizenship and immigration status requirement, aged, blind or disabled, and within the SSI resource standard.

Precision. 'Meets SSI eligibility criteria except for the level of their income' is read as residency, status (CO-509), aged, blind or disabled (CO-603) and the SSI resource standard (CO-610); the SSI income standard is not tested, so an OAP grant above the SSI federal benefit rate does not defeat it. § 8.100.3.M.2.b names only OAP "A" for code B while § 8.100.6.K.4 names OAP-A and OAP-B; af_category carries a single OAP category, so both are read (OQ-206). OAP recipients who lost OAP to a non-OASDI cost of living adjustment (§ 8.100.6.K.7) are SISC C, not SISC B, so this item reads current OAP receipt only; ma_oap_health_care_status (CO-1156) brings them in through ma_lost_oap_to_non_oasdi_cost_of_living_adjustment (OQ-206, resolved).

### CO-1185 Medicaid: months over which lottery or gambling winnings are spread `@engine`

The number of months over which the person's lottery or gambling winnings are divided equally and counted as MAGI income - 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.4.C.1.b.xiv.1-3: one month (the month received) for winnings of $79,999 or less; two months for winnings over $79,999 up to $89,999; and one more month for each further $10,000 or part of it.

Precision. Computed as 1 + the number of $10,000 increments (a part increment counting as one) by which the winnings exceed $79,999: $80,000 to $89,999 gives 2 months, $90,000 to $99,999 gives 3, $100,000 to $109,999 gives 4. § 8.100.4.C.1.b.xiv.3's 'for every additional $10,000 over $89,999' is read as each started $10,000 band above $89,999, which matches the federal rule's $10,000 increments; a reading that adds a month only for each full $10,000 over $89,999 would give 2 months up to $99,999 (OQ-216). OQ-216 sweep: the federal thresholds are $80,000, $90,000 and $100,000 with one more month for each $10,000 increment (42 U.S.C. 1396a(e)(14)(K)(i), S1234), which this reading matches at every boundary ($79,999 is one month, $89,999 two, $99,999 three, $100,000 four); Colorado's text states no upper limit, but the statute caps the period at 120 months (ma_lottery_winnings_spread_max_months, reached at $1,260,000).

Type whole number, scope person, program Medicaid.
Uses: `lottery_gambling_winnings_amount`, `ma_lottery_winnings_spread_floor`, `ma_lottery_winnings_spread_increment`, `ma_lottery_winnings_spread_max_months`.

```
if Lottery or gambling winnings amount is at most Medicaid: lottery and gambling winnings counted only in the month received, upper amount (79999)
  then 1
otherwise the lesser of Lottery winnings spread, maximum months (120) and 1 plus ((Lottery or gambling winnings amount minus Medicaid: lottery and gambling winnings counted only in the month received, upper amount (79999)) divided by Medicaid: lottery and gambling winnings amount that adds a month of spreading (10000) rounded up to the next whole dollar)
```

```json
["case",[["<=","lottery_gambling_winnings_amount","ma_lottery_winnings_spread_floor"],1],["else",["min","ma_lottery_winnings_spread_max_months",["+",1,["ceil",["/",["-","lottery_gambling_winnings_amount","ma_lottery_winnings_spread_floor"],"ma_lottery_winnings_spread_increment"]]]]]]
```

### CO-1415 Medicaid: verification status `@engine`

Where this person's Medical Assistance verification stands: not applicable (coverage is not requested for the person); none required; complete; pending within the time allowed; past the time allowed with documentation other than status outstanding; only citizenship, identity or immigration status outstanding within the reasonable opportunity period (benefits are furnished meanwhile to an otherwise eligible person); or the reasonable opportunity period expired with status unverified.

Precision. past_due and reasonable_opportunity_expired state that the time allowed has run; the termination itself (within 30 days, with notice) is processing outside this item. An extension of the time to verify (§ 8.100.3.D.2) or of the reasonable opportunity period for a good faith effort (§ 8.100.3.H.10) moves the due date and the period's end (CO-1414, CO-1413; OQ-316, resolved for Medical Assistance). Medical Assistance's own request fact (ma_is_requesting_coverage) is read before the shared one (OQ-382). At a renewal the renewal form allows at least 30 days (435.916(a)(3)(i)(B)), the same period ma_verification_due_date uses.

Type one of, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `is_requesting_health_coverage`, `ma_is_requesting_coverage`, `ma_pending_status_verification_count`, `ma_pending_verification_count`, `ma_reasonable_opportunity_period_end_date`, `ma_required_verification_count`, `ma_verification_due_date`.

```
if it is not the case that Medical Assistance is requested for the person, otherwise Requesting health coverage
  then not_applicable
else if Medicaid: required verification count is equal to 0
  then not_required
else if Medicaid: pending verification count is equal to 0
  then complete
else if all of the following are true:
    - (Medicaid: pending verification count minus Medicaid: pending status verification count) is more than 0
    - the Determination Date is more than Medicaid: verification due date
  then past_due
else if all of the following are true:
    - Medicaid: pending status verification count is more than 0
    - the Determination Date is more than Medicaid: reasonable opportunity period end date
  then reasonable_opportunity_expired
else if (Medicaid: pending verification count minus Medicaid: pending status verification count) is more than 0
  then pending
otherwise pending_reasonable_opportunity
```

```json
["case",[["not",["otherwise","ma_is_requesting_coverage","is_requesting_health_coverage"]],"not_applicable"],[["=","ma_required_verification_count",0],"not_required"],[["=","ma_pending_verification_count",0],"complete"],[["all",[">",["-","ma_pending_verification_count","ma_pending_status_verification_count"],0],[">",["det_date"],"ma_verification_due_date"]],"past_due"],[["all",[">","ma_pending_status_verification_count",0],[">",["det_date"],"ma_reasonable_opportunity_period_end_date"]],"reasonable_opportunity_expired"],[[">",["-","ma_pending_verification_count","ma_pending_status_verification_count"],0],"pending"],["else","pending_reasonable_opportunity"]]
```

### CO-1640 Medical Assistance: aged, blind and disabled income is reasonably compatible `@engine`

Whether an aged, blind or disabled applicant's attested monthly income is reasonably compatible with the electronic data source's figure, judged against the applicable income standard: both at or below it, both above it, or the attested figure at or below it and the data no more than 20% above the attested figure. For a long-term care applicant the figures are gross income and the standard is 300% of the SSI individual rate (the special income group); for any other aged, blind or disabled applicant they are SSI-related countable income (ma_ssi_countable_income, and ma_ssi_countable_income_reported_by_data_source for the data) and the standard is the SSI rate for the household size, the couple rate for a couple (ma_ssi_income_standard).

The countable comparison applies the same $20, $65 and one-half disregards to both figures and combines a spouse living with the person (OQ-374, resolved). ### CO-1704 Medicaid: net earnings from self-employment (non-MAGI) `@engine`

The person's net profit from self-employment for the month for the non-MAGI Medical Assistance groups (SSI-related, Buy-In, long-term care, spousal allowances): gross receipts less the cost of doing business 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.3.K.9 allows, not below zero.

Precision. MAGI-based income reads the federal tax figure (self_employment_net_earnings_for_tax, CO-024) instead, because 8.100.3.K.9.b.i.1 allows depreciation for MAGI only. The SSI method's offset of a self-employment loss against wages (20 CFR 416.1111(b)) is not modeled; the net is floored at zero. A person with no gross receipts has none, whatever the cost fact says.

Uses: `ma_self_employment_business_costs`, `self_employment_gross_receipts`.

```
  then 0
otherwise the greater of 0 and Self-employment gross receipts minus Medicaid: cost of doing business for self-employment
```

Precision. Former foster care is read through ma_is_former_foster_care_category (CO-549), which states the 1902(a)(10)(A)(i)(IX) group without the turned-18-after-2023 condition, as 435.554(c)(1) directs. Postpartum entitlement under 1902(e)(5) or (16) is read through ma_is_in_pregnancy_coverage_period (CO-566). Participation in a treatment program reads participates_in_drug_alcohol_treatment (CO-045), whose meaning is the 7 U.S.C. 2012(h) program 435.554(c)(8) adopts; Colorado states no minimum time commitment (OQ-412). ### CO-1974 Medicaid community engagement status `@engine`

The community engagement result for the person at this determination under 42 CFR 435.550-435.559: not_assessed (no application, renewal or change-in-circumstances review at this determination, including an enrolled beneficiary before the first renewal on or after the implementation date, 435.559(c)); excluded (a specified excluded individual in the determination month, so not an applicable individual, 435.551, 435.554(b)); met (at application, every month of the look-back met; at renewal or a change-in-circumstances redetermination, at least ma_community_engagement_renewal_required_months months met); or not_met.

Precision. The result is the same for every month of the determination; it is stated per month so the look-back can read each month assessed. Specified excluded status is tested in the determination month; in a look-back month it is a mandatory exception (435.553(a)(4)), so a person excluded in some look-back months and not now still meets those months. The noncompliance procedures of 435.558 (a 30-day notice period, continued coverage until a determination of ineligibility, and consideration of every other basis of eligibility) and the verification rules of 435.557 are not modeled: not_met is the result once the information is in, not the notice that precedes it.

Type one of, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `ma_community_engagement_renewal_required_months`, `ma_community_engagement_review_months`, `ma_community_engagement_review_type`, `ma_is_specified_excluded_individual`, `ma_meets_community_engagement_for_month`.

```
if Community engagement review type is equal to none
  then not_assessed
else if Medicaid community engagement: is a specified excluded individual for the month containing the Determination Date
  then excluded
else if Community engagement review type is equal to application
  then (if in each of Medicaid community engagement: months assessed:;     Medicaid community engagement: met for the month for the month;   then met; otherwise not_met)
else if (the number of months in Medicaid community engagement: months assessed for which Medicaid community engagement: met for the month for the month) is at least Medicaid community engagement: months required at renewal (1)
  then met
otherwise not_met
```

### CO-2205 Medicaid: a continuous eligibility exception applies `@engine`

Whether, this month, one of the exceptions of 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.3.Q.1.b ends (or, for an inmate, suspends) a child's continuous eligibility period other than the residency exception, which ma_child_is_in_continuous_eligibility_period (CO-561) tests itself: the child has died (i); is an inmate of a public institution (ii); is no longer part of the Medical Assistance required household (iii); is unable to be located (v); has requested withdrawal (vi); failed to provide documentation during a reasonable opportunity period (vii); or the eligibility was erroneously granted through agency error, fraud or perjury (viii).

Precision. The period ends 'effective the earliest possible month', so each month fact is read as true from the month of the event on. An inmate's coverage moves to the limited incarceration benefit and full coverage is reinstated for the rest of the period on release (Q.1.b.ii.1), so the inmate prong reads the month's own inmate status (is_inmate_of_public_institution, CO-1105) and the period resumes in a later month the child is not an inmate. Exception vii is read from the volume's reasonable opportunity items: a month after the month the reasonable opportunity period ended (ma_reasonable_opportunity_period_end_date) with citizenship, identity or immigration status still pending (ma_pending_status_verification_count). A person to whom no reasonable opportunity notice was sent (ma_reasonable_opportunity_notice_date not stated) had no reasonable opportunity period and cannot fail to provide documentation during one, so the prong is false for that person.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `is_deceased`, `is_inmate_of_public_institution`, `ma_eligibility_was_erroneously_granted`, `ma_has_left_required_household`, `ma_has_requested_withdrawal_from_continuous_eligibility`, `ma_is_unable_to_be_located`, `ma_pending_status_verification_count`, `ma_reasonable_opportunity_period_end_date`.

```
any of the following is true:
  - Is deceased
  - Is an inmate of a public institution
  - Has left the Medical Assistance required household
  - Is unable to be located
  - Has requested withdrawal from continuous eligibility
  - Eligibility was erroneously granted
  - all of the following are true:
    - the month is more than the month containing Medicaid: reasonable opportunity period end date, otherwise no
    - Medicaid: pending status verification count is more than 0
```

```json
["any","is_deceased","is_inmate_of_public_institution","ma_has_left_required_household","ma_is_unable_to_be_located","ma_has_requested_withdrawal_from_continuous_eligibility","ma_eligibility_was_erroneously_granted",["all",["otherwise",[">",["month"],["month_of","ma_reasonable_opportunity_period_end_date"]],false],[">","ma_pending_status_verification_count",0]]]
```

### CO-2238 Medicaid: income trust monthly distribution `@engine`

The amount an income trust distributes this month for the person (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.7, income trusts, 6.a.i.b and f): for a Long-Term Care institution member, the entire income transferred into the trust less the amount retained for trust expenses (at most $20); for an HCBS member, the same, but no more than 300% of the SSI limit, the rest remaining in the trust.

Precision. The trust holds all of the person's monthly income (pension, Social Security and other income, 6.a.i), so the income transferred in is ma_ltc_gross_income. ### CO-2241 Medicaid: SSI-related countable income reported by electronic data `@engine`

The SSI-related countable income the electronic data sources report for the person and a spouse living with the person: the reported unearned income less the $20 general income disregard, plus the reported earned income less the $65 earned income disregard and any unused part of the $20, halved - the computation ma_ssi_countable_income makes from the attested figures (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.5.H.4.a-b; 20 CFR 416.1124(c)(12)).

Precision. Reported unearned income is the reported gross income less its earned part (electronic_data_source_monthly_earned_income); both are summed over the same spouse-living-together group ma_ssi_household_unearned_income_sum (CO-663) uses. The Ineligible Child Allocation and an unemancipated child's child support (CO-2281) are not applied: the data sources report income, not the household's children or SSI status, so the comparison with ma_ssi_countable_income can differ by the allocation in a household with ineligible children.

### CO-2250 Medicaid: meets the residency requirement `@engine`

Whether the person is a resident of Colorado for Medical Assistance (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.3.B.2-5; 42 CFR 435.403): a person living in Colorado who considers it the place of residence, including one temporarily absent who intends to return (is_colorado_resident); or, for a person in an institution who is incapable of indicating intent, Colorado is the state of residence the institutional rules give (ma_institutionalized_state_of_residence).

Precision. state_of_residence, which is_colorado_resident reads, is the state the person lives in and intends to remain in, so a person temporarily absent with intent to return (B.4) is stated with Colorado and a person who intends to return to a home outside Colorado (§ 8.100.5.M.2.a.iii) is not. Federal residency for a person receiving a State supplementary payment (the paying State, 435.403(f)) and for a title IV-E child (the State where the child lives, 435.403(g)) is not restated by Colorado and not modeled.

Uses: `colorado_state_code`, `is_colorado_resident`, `ma_institutionalized_state_of_residence`, `ma_is_incapable_of_indicating_intent`, `resides_in_medical_institution`.

```
if all of the following are true:
    - Is incapable of indicating intent, otherwise no
    - Resides in a medical institution
  then Medicaid: state of residence of an institutionalized person incapable of indicating intent is equal to Colorado state code (CO)
otherwise Is a Colorado resident
```

### CO-2257 Medicaid: state of residence of an institutionalized person incapable of indicating intent `@engine`

The state of residence, as a two-letter code, of a person in an institution who is incapable of indicating intent (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.3.B.2; 42 CFR 435.403(e), (h)(3)-(4)): the state that arranged the placement, when a state placed the person in an institution in another state (B.2.c); otherwise, for a person under 21 or who became incapable before 21, the state of the parents or guardian at the time of placement (B.2.a); otherwise the state where the institution is located (B.2 and B.2.c, where the person is physically present).

Precision. For a person who became incapable at or after 21, § 8.100.3.B.2.b names 'the state in which the person was living when he or she became incapable of indicating intent', while B.2.c and 42 CFR 435.403(h)(4) name the state where the person is placed and physically present; the draft follows B.2.c and the federal rule (OQ-472).

Type text, scope person, program Medicaid.
Uses: `age`, `ma_became_incapable_of_indicating_intent_before_age_twenty_one`, `ma_institution_state`, `ma_institutional_placement_arranging_state`, `ma_parent_or_guardian_state_at_placement`, `ma_residency_parental_state_age_limit`, `ma_was_placed_in_institution_by_a_state`.

```
if Was placed in an institution by a state
  then State that arranged the institutional placement
else if any of the following is true:
    - Age is less than Medicaid residency parental-state age limit (21)
    - Became incapable of indicating intent before age 21
  then Parent's or guardian's state at placement
otherwise State where the institution is located
```

### CO-2270 Medicaid: meets the designated HCBS waiver's condition criteria `@engine`

False when no waiver is designated.

Precision. The age criteria are ma_hcbs_waiver_age_criteria_met (CO-1164) and the level of care ma_meets_designated_waiver_level_of_care (CO-1178); CwCHN's hospital level-of-care conditions are part of the level of care. BI's onset is compared as the whole years from birth to the injury date.

The total Ineligible Child Allocation for the person's SSI-related household (the person and a spouse living with the person): for each child of either who is an unemancipated child in the home and is not applying for or eligible for SSI, one half of the SSI individual Federal Benefit Rate, reduced by the child's own gross income (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.5.H.3.a.i, H.2.a-b).

Precision. The child's own income is gross earned and unearned income, child support included in full, since the one-third reduction of § 8.100.5.H.4.c 'does not apply to ineligible children when calculating the ineligible child allocation disregard'. A child is in the home through the parent edge, the volume's convention for living together.

### CO-500 Medicaid: MAGI household members `@engine`

This person's MAGI household under 42 CFR 435.603(f) and 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.4.E.1 - a tax filer not claimed as a dependent's household is the filer, the filer's spouse, and everyone the filer claims as a tax dependent; a claimed tax dependent's household is the claiming filer's household, unless the filer claiming them is someone other than their spouse or parent, in which case (and for a true non-filer) the household is the non-filer household of that person, their spouse, their children under ma_magi_child_age_limit, and, if this person is themselves under that age, their own parents and siblings under that age living with them.

Precision. Household membership is symmetric within the case model but each person's own value of this item is their own household, per 8.100.4.E's per-applicant test. A claimed dependent who meets any exception of 435.603(f)(2)(i)-(iii) or § 8.100.4.E.5 (ma_dependent_is_routed_to_non_filer_rules, CO-1976, OQ-42 resolved) has the non-filer household. In the non-filer household only persons in this person's lives_with (CO-1925) are counted, so a parent outside the home (a non-custodial parent, or the parent living apart under E.5) is not; where lives_with is not stated, 'living with' is read from the case's stated relationships (a spouse, parent/child, or tax_filer/tax_dependent edge being stated at all is read as living together/claiming, matching this volume's snap_household_members convention of crossing a stated spouse edge unconditionally). 'Siblings' is read through the engine's shared_relative pattern (P43, docs/conventions.md), which finds the persons who share a parent edge with this person directly - not by re-walking the parent-then-child chain that over-included an unrelated person in this item's earlier draft (see the batch-6 report).

### CO-502 Medicaid: person's MAGI-based income `@engine`

This person's own MAGI-based income for the month under 42 CFR 435.603(e) and 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.4.C - taxable earned and unearned income (including Social Security benefits, whether or not taxable, capital gains, lottery and gambling winnings in the month received, and countable discharged student loan debt), plus tax-exempt interest and excluded foreign earned income added back in, minus above-the-line pretax deductions (including pre-tax 401(k)/403(b) contributions, net operating losses and capital losses).

Precision. Monthly amount for the month in context. Child support received, Supplemental Security Income, and TANF cash assistance are excluded per § 8.100.4.C.1.d; a lump sum is counted only in the month received (§ 8.100.4.C.1.d.i and 435.603(e)(1)) - this item reads its supplied income facts as already stating that convention, per this volume's shared income-fact meanings - except lottery and gambling winnings over $79,999, which § 8.100.4.C.1.b.xiv spreads over two or more months for the winner: this item counts winnings in the month received (ma_lottery_winnings_counted_in_month_received, CO-1186), which is how they count for the other members of the winner's household (xiv.4), and ma_magi_household_income (CO-503) substitutes the spread amount when the household is the winner's own. Capital gains (xiii) are in magi_other_taxable_income (CO-079); discharged student loan debt (xv) is ma_countable_discharged_student_loan_income (CO-1190), not magi_other_taxable_income or other_unearned_income_nontaxable; pre-tax 401(k) or 403(b) contributions, net operating losses and capital losses (§ 8.100.4.C.1.e.viii, xiii-xv) are in pretax_deductions (CO-080), since wages_gross (CO-023) is gross wages. Rounded to the nearest dollar following this volume's snap_household_gross_income convention (halves up), since no MAGI-specific rounding election is stated in the cited text. Phase 7 fix round (S-9) added the winnings and student loan terms. Vocabulary fix round (R-1): reads the taxable part of other unearned income (other_unearned_income_taxable, CO-1714); the non-taxable part (gifts and contributions, veterans' benefits, workers' compensation; other_unearned_income_nontaxable, CO-030) is not MAGI income (8.100.4.C.1.d). Self-employment is the federal tax figure (self_employment_net_earnings_for_tax, CO-024).

Type money, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `foreign_earned_income_excluded`, `ma_countable_discharged_student_loan_income`, `ma_lottery_winnings_counted_in_month_received`, `magi_other_taxable_income`, `other_unearned_income_taxable`, `pension_income`, `pretax_deductions`, `self_employment_net_earnings_for_tax`, `social_security_income`, `tax_exempt_interest`, `unemployment_income`, `wages_gross`.

```
(Gross wages plus Net earnings from self-employment for federal income tax plus MAGI: other taxable income not received as unearned income plus Social Security income plus Pension income plus Unemployment income plus Other unearned income, federally taxable plus Tax-exempt interest plus Excluded foreign earned income plus Medicaid: lottery or gambling winnings counted in the month received plus Medicaid: countable discharged student loan income) minus Pretax deductions rounded to the nearest whole dollar
```

### CO-503 Medicaid: MAGI household income `@engine`

This person's MAGI household's total countable income for the month under 42 CFR 435.603(d) and 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.4.C.1.f - the sum of each household member's own ma_person_magi_income, except that a member's income is left out when the member is expected to be claimed as a tax dependent and is not required to file a tax return.

Precision. Sums over ma_magi_household_members. A member's income is excluded only when the member is not required to file a tax return AND either (a) 435.603(d)(2)(i): someone in THIS household (the group being summed, read as a bare `ma_magi_household_members`, not the member's own independently-computed household) is that member's parent, or (b) 435.603(d)(2)(ii): the member is a dependent claimed by someone other than a spouse or parent (ma_is_dependent_claimed_by_non_parent, CO-563). Clause (a) is deliberately evaluated against the SUMMING household, not the member's own ma_magi_household_members value: 8.100.4.C.1.f.iii states 'the income of a child or tax dependent who does not live with their natural, adopted, or step parent will always count towards the determination of their own eligibility' - and 'their own eligibility' is decided per household, so a dependent whose parent is not a member of THIS particular household (for example a grandchild's non-filer household that excludes the claiming grandparent's own household) counts fully here even though the same dependent's income is excluded when the parent IS a co-member of a different household being summed. Fix round: replaced the prior expects_to_be_claimed_as_dependent proxy, which both over- and under-counted relative to this test, per the phase-3 review's C-6 finding. A member's income is excluded only when the member is not required to file and either a parent of the member, or the non-parent who claims the member, is in the household being summed (P45); so a child with no parent in her own household counts her own income, as 8.100.4.C.1.f.iii requires. Phase 7 fix round (S-9): each member's income counts lottery or gambling winnings only in the month received (CO-502, § 8.100.4.C.1.b.xiv.4); for this person's own winnings the household total then swaps that for the amount spread over months (ma_lottery_winnings_countable_for_recipient, CO-1187, xiv.1-3). The swap assumes this person's own income is counted in the household, which holds for anyone with winnings large enough to spread (they must file a return); it is not made conditional on the exclusion clauses above.

Type money, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `is_required_to_file_tax_return`, `ma_is_dependent_claimed_by_non_parent`, `ma_lottery_winnings_countable_for_recipient`, `ma_lottery_winnings_counted_in_month_received`, `ma_magi_household_members`, `ma_person_magi_income`, `relationships`.

```
(the sum of that person's Medicaid: person's MAGI-based income for each person in all persons in Medicaid: MAGI household members such that it is not the case that (all of the following are true:;   - it is not the case that that person's Is required to file a tax return;   - any of the following is true:;     - that person is a child of a person in Medicaid: MAGI household members;     - all of the following are true:;       - that person is a tax_dependent of a person in Medicaid: MAGI household members;       - that person's Medicaid: is a dependent claimed by someone other than a spouse or parent)) plus (Medicaid: lottery or gambling winnings counted for the winner this month minus Medicaid: lottery or gambling winnings counted in the month received) rounded to the nearest whole dollar
```

### CO-509 Medicaid: meets the citizenship requirement `@engine`

Whether the person falls into one of the citizenship and immigration status categories of 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.3.G.1.g (and 42 CFR 435.406(a)) that admit a person to full Medical Assistance: a citizen or national (i); a qualified non-citizen who has held the status for five years (iii) or is exempt from the five-year rule (iv-v, ma_is_five_year_bar_exempt, CO-1172); or a lawfully residing non-citizen who is a pregnant woman or a child under 19 (vii, the CHIPRA 214 option). The Cover All Coloradans exception (ix.1) is not part of this test: it reaches only the categories ix.1.a-b list, which read ma_meets_status_for_cover_all_coloradans_categories (CO-1174) instead.

Precision. The five-year rule is counted from qualified_status_date (has_held_qualified_status_five_years, CO-508); § 8.100.3.G.1.g.iii counts it from the date of entry, which for a person admitted directly as a Lawful Permanent Resident is the same date. The lawfully residing arm (vii) reads ma_is_lawfully_present (CO-507), which includes every qualified non-citizen, so a Lawful Permanent Resident inside the five-year rule who is pregnant or under 19 meets status through vii ("falls into one of the categories listed in Section 8.100.3.G.1.g.iii ... not subject to the five-year rule"), as the text states; the age is read strictly as "under the age of 19 years". ii (a lawfully residing non-citizen who entered before August 22, 1996) is not modeled, because no fact states the date of entry (phase-3 K-2). viii (Afghan humanitarian parolees) exempted parolees only until March 31, 2023 or the end of parole; not modeled. Phase 7 fix round: B-1 limited the lawfully present arm to pregnant women and children, as vii states; B-2 replaced the veteran-only exemption with CO-1172; S-2 moved the Cover All Coloradans disjuncts to ma_is_cover_all_coloradans_person (CO-1173). See OQ-213 and OQ-214. Vocabulary fix round (U-3): the citizen-or-national arm reads is_us_citizen_or_national (CO-1358).

Type yes/no, scope person, program Medicaid.
Uses: `age`, `has_held_qualified_status_five_years`, `is_pregnant`, `is_qualified_non_citizen`, `is_us_citizen_or_national`, `ma_is_five_year_bar_exempt`, `ma_is_lawfully_present`, `ma_magi_child_age_limit`.

```
  - Is a U.S. citizen or national
  - all of the following are true:
    - Is a qualified non-citizen
    - any of the following is true:

  - all of the following are true:

      - Age is less than MAGI household child age limit (19)
```

### CO-510 Medicaid: is emergency Medicaid only `@engine`

Whether the person fails citizenship and immigration requirements but meets every other requirement of a categorical Medical Assistance program (ma_meets_requirements_other_than_status, CO-1150), and so is limited to emergency medical services (and reproductive health care) under 42 CFR 435.406(b), 42 U.S.C. 1396b(v) and 10 CCR 2505-10 §§ 8.100.3.F.1.k and 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.2 (numbered viii.2 in the Cornell copy, D-39), rather than full Medical Assistance benefits.

Precision. A person who fails the status test (CO-509) is emergency-only when every other requirement of a categorical program is met (ma_meets_requirements_other_than_status, CO-1150: residency, the institution for mental diseases requirement, and a MAGI category, the SSI-related standards, OAP SISC B, or institutional long-term care) and the person is not fully covered through Cover All Coloradans in a category § 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.1.a-b lists (ma_is_covered_under_cover_all_coloradans, CO-1175). So an undocumented child in the Children's category is fully covered, not emergency-only, while an undocumented postpartum adult whose only category is Adult is emergency-only (phase 7 fix round, S-2). A person who meets no category, or is over every income standard, is not emergency-only; ma_magi_eligibility_status (CO-554) reports ineligible_income for that person. The emergency-only benefit is itself limited to a true emergency medical condition (including labor and delivery); this item states eligibility for the coverage category, and ma_emergency_medicaid_status (CO-1151) reads the month's emergency medical condition.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `ma_is_covered_under_cover_all_coloradans`, `ma_meets_citizenship_requirement`, `ma_meets_requirements_other_than_status`.

```
all of the following are true:
  - it is not the case that Medicaid: meets the citizenship requirement
  - it is not the case that Medicaid: is covered under Cover All Coloradans
  - Medicaid: meets every requirement other than citizenship or immigration status
```

```json
["all",["not","ma_meets_citizenship_requirement"],["not","ma_is_covered_under_cover_all_coloradans"],"ma_meets_requirements_other_than_status"]
```

### CO-539 Medicaid: highest MAGI income standard the person could qualify under `@engine`

The greatest MAGI income standard, as a decimal fraction of FPL, among the covered groups whose non-income (demographic) criteria this person meets this month - the standard 42 CFR 435.603(d)(4) means by "the eligibility group with the highest income standard" for the 5% disregard.

Precision. Tests each of the four income-tested groups' own non-income criteria directly (not their full category rules, which already fold in the income test the disregard would otherwise be deciding), and takes the greatest of the standards for the groups the person could qualify under, 0 for the rest, via P40 (the greater of two numbers, nested). The Former Foster Care and Needy Newborn groups take no income test at all (8.100.4.H.2.b, 8.100.4.G.7) and so never bound the disregard; they are not inputs to this item.

Type rate, scope person-month, program Medicaid.

