### CO-545 Medicaid: meets the Children MAGI category `@engine`

Whether the person meets the Children's MAGI Medical Assistance category under 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.4.G.2 - under ma_magi_child_age_limit (19), with household income at or below ma_magi_income_standard_child, applying the 5% income disregard of 42 CFR 435.603(d)(4) and 8.100.4.D as the last step only if income above the plain standard would otherwise make the person ineligible.

Precision. The disregard test subtracts ma_magi_income_disregard_pct (a percentage of the poverty guideline) from ma_magi_household_income_pct_fpl and compares the result to the same standard, per 8.100.4.D.1.a's "as the last step to determine eligibility"; it is not applied when income already meets the plain standard, per 8.100.4.D.1.b. Per 42 CFR 435.603(d)(4), which permits the disregard "only ... for the eligibility group with the highest income standard ... but not to determine eligibility for a particular eligibility group," the disregard disjunct here is further gated on ma_magi_income_standard_child actually being this person's highest standard (ma_magi_highest_income_standard_pct, CO-539, fix round) - the phase-3 review's C-2 finding.

      - (Medicaid: MAGI household income as a percentage of the poverty guideline minus MAGI income disregard percentage (0.05)) is at most Medicaid: MAGI Children category income standard

### CO-547 Medicaid: meets the Parents and Caretaker Relatives MAGI category `@engine`

Whether the person meets the Parents and Caretaker Relatives MAGI Medical Assistance category under 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.4.G.3 - a parent or caretaker relative of a dependent child living with them, with household income at or below ma_income_limit_parent_caretaker_pct, applying the 5% income disregard of 42 CFR 435.603(d)(4) and 8.100.4.D as the last step only if income above the plain standard would otherwise make the person ineligible.

Precision. 'Living with them' is read from the case's stated parent or caretaker relationship edge, per this volume's convention (see ma_magi_household_members, CO-500) that a stated relationship edge is read as living together. 'Parent or caretaker relative' reads the case's parent and caretaker relationship roles; no degree of relation is tested because Colorado's definition takes 42 CFR 435.4's State option (3): a Caretaker Relative is 'a person who is related to the dependent child or any adult with whom the dependent child is living and who assumes responsibility for the dependent child's care' (§ 8.100.1, S1500), so any relative, and any adult living with the child who assumes responsibility for the child's care, qualifies; a caretaker edge states exactly that (OQ-51, resolved). Per 42 CFR 435.603(d)(4), the disregard disjunct is gated on ma_income_limit_parent_caretaker_pct being this person's highest standard (ma_magi_highest_income_standard_pct, CO-539, fix round) - the phase-3 review's C-2 finding: it is available here only for a person the Adults group is closed to (65+, Medicare-entitled), not for every parent/caretaker between 60% and 65% of FPL, who is placed in the Adults group instead. Dropped the minimum-essential-coverage condition on the dependent child in the fix round: 8.100.4.G.3 states only the dependent-child relationship, with no MEC condition; the MEC condition belongs to the Adults category (8.100.4.G.4.a, 42 CFR 435.119(c)(1)) - the phase-3 review's C-3 finding.

### CO-548 Medicaid: meets the Adults MAGI category `@engine`

Whether the person meets the Adults MAGI Medical Assistance category under 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.4.G.4 and 42 CFR 435.119(b) - age ma_magi_child_age_limit (19) through under ma_adult_upper_age_limit (65), not pregnant, not entitled to or enrolled in Medicare, not otherwise eligible under the Children's, Pregnant Women, or Parents/Caretaker Relatives categories, any dependent child under 19 in the person's household as a parent or caretaker relative has minimum essential coverage, with household income at or below ma_magi_income_standard_adult, applying the 5% income disregard of 42 CFR 435.603(d)(4) and 8.100.4.D as the last step only if income above the plain standard would otherwise make the person ineligible.

Precision. 8.100.4.G.4 also folds in a parent or caretaker relative whose income exceeds the Parents/Caretaker standard but who otherwise meets this category's own criteria (income at or below 133%), which this rule reaches automatically since it does not exclude someone for having a dependent child, only for already qualifying under ma_is_parent_caretaker_category. This batch does not separately model the Former Foster Care category as a 435.119(b)(4) exclusion because 435.150(b)(2) instead makes Former Foster Care itself conditional on not being eligible under 435.110-435.145 (the mandatory groups including Adults); this rule's own mandatory-group exclusions (Children's, Pregnant Women, Parents/Caretaker) are the ones 435.119(b)(4) names. The minimum-essential-coverage condition is added in the fix round, moved here from CO-547 per the phase-3 review's C-3 finding: 8.100.4.G.4.a and 42 CFR 435.119(c)(1) condition Adults eligibility, not Parents/Caretaker eligibility, on a dependent child in the parent/caretaker relative's household having MEC. The age is under 19 (ma_magi_child_age_limit), per 435.119(c)(2), not the parent/caretaker category's own 18/18-in-school dependent-child age (ma_dependent_child_age_limit, CO-190) - the negative-condition form 435.119(c)(1) states: the person fails this category only if there IS a dependent child under 19 in the household without MEC. Per 42 CFR 435.603(d)(4), the disregard disjunct is gated on ma_magi_income_standard_adult being this person's highest standard (ma_magi_highest_income_standard_pct, CO-539, fix round) - the phase-3 review's C-2 finding. This item states the group criteria of 435.119(b)-(c); the community engagement requirement 435.119(d) adds from January 1, 2027 is ma_meets_adult_group_community_engagement_condition (CO-1975), which ma_magi_category (CO-551) applies together with this item (OQ-65).

### CO-551 Medicaid: MAGI covered group `@engine`

Which MAGI Medical Assistance covered group, if any, the person qualifies under this month, evaluated under 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.4.G's mandatory groups - needy newborn, children, pregnant women, parents and caretaker relatives, former foster care children, and adults - or "none" if the person qualifies under none of them.

Precision. Evaluated in the order 8.100.4.G lists the mandatory groups, with needy newborn checked first because 8.100.4.G.7 grants it without an income test and it can otherwise overlap with the Children's category for an infant under 1; each subsequent category's own test already excludes anyone who qualified under an earlier-listed category (see ma_is_adult_category, CO-548, and ma_is_former_foster_care_category's federal basis, 435.150(b)(2)), so a person who could qualify under more than one category is placed in the first (highest-priority) one this case expression checks, not necessarily the one with the highest income standard. A child in an open continuous eligibility period (ma_child_is_in_continuous_eligibility_period, CO-561, fix round) is reported 'child' ahead of the ordinary category tests, per 42 CFR 435.926(d)/10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.3.Q.1.a's 'without regard to changes in income' rule (the phase-3 review's C-4(a) finding) - but only when the person is not a needy newborn, so a newborn who is also in a CE period (opened by an older sibling's application, for example) still reports needy_newborn, the stronger unconditional entitlement. From January 1, 2027 the Adults group also requires the community engagement condition of 42 CFR 435.119(d) (ma_meets_adult_group_community_engagement_condition, CO-1975, OQ-65): a person who meets the Adults criteria (CO-548) but not the condition is reported none, and ma_magi_eligibility_status (CO-554) gives the reason.

Type one of, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `ma_child_is_in_continuous_eligibility_period`, `ma_is_adult_category`, `ma_is_child_category`, `ma_is_former_foster_care_category`, `ma_is_in_pregnancy_coverage_period`, `ma_is_needy_newborn`, `ma_is_parent_caretaker_category`, `ma_is_pregnant_category`, `ma_meets_adult_group_community_engagement_condition`.

```
if Medicaid: is an Eligible Needy Newborn
  then needy_newborn
else if Medicaid: child is in a continuous eligibility period
  then child
else if Medicaid: meets the Children MAGI category
  then child
else if Medicaid: is in the pregnancy coverage period
  then pregnant
else if Medicaid: meets the Pregnant Women MAGI category
  then pregnant
else if Medicaid: meets the Parents and Caretaker Relatives MAGI category
  then parent_caretaker
else if Medicaid: meets the Former Foster Care Children category
  then former_foster_care
else if all of the following are true:
    - Medicaid: meets the Adults MAGI category
    - Medicaid: Adults group community engagement condition
  then adult
otherwise none
```

```json
["case",["ma_is_needy_newborn","needy_newborn"],["ma_child_is_in_continuous_eligibility_period","child"],["ma_is_child_category","child"],["ma_is_in_pregnancy_coverage_period","pregnant"],["ma_is_pregnant_category","pregnant"],["ma_is_parent_caretaker_category","parent_caretaker"],["ma_is_former_foster_care_category","former_foster_care"],[["all","ma_is_adult_category","ma_meets_adult_group_community_engagement_condition"],"adult"],["else","none"]]
```

### CO-554 Medicaid: MAGI eligibility status `@engine`

The reason code for the person's MAGI Medical Assistance eligibility this month - full eligibility, emergency-Medicaid-only, ineligible because the person meets the Adults group criteria but not the community engagement requirement that conditions that group from January 1, 2027 (42 CFR 435.119(d)), ineligible because household income exceeds every category the person could otherwise fit, ineligible because the person is not a Colorado resident, or ineligible because the person fits no MAGI category's demographic requirements at all.

Precision. Residency is checked first because it is a threshold requirement of every category; a child in an open continuous eligibility period (ma_child_is_in_continuous_eligibility_period, CO-561, fix round) is reported eligible next, per 42 CFR 435.926(d)/10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.3.Q.1.a's 'without regard to changes in income' rule (the phase-3 review's C-4(a) finding) - checked ahead of emergency-only and the income/no-category branches so a CE period is not defeated by a later citizenship or income change; emergency-only is checked next because 8.100.3.G.1.g.viii.2 (S175) grants it to a resident who fails citizenship but otherwise meets the plan's requirements, matching ma_is_emergency_medicaid_only's own scope (CO-510, edited in the fix round per C-11 to require a category); Phase 7: the emergency-only branch also requires a MAGI category, because ma_is_emergency_medicaid_only (CO-510) now covers the SSI-related and long-term care routes too, and this is the MAGI status (the cross-chapter emergency determination is ma_emergency_medicaid_status, CO-1151); the income/no-category distinction (ma_meets_some_category_demographics, CO-552) is checked last, only once residency, continuous eligibility, and citizenship are settled.

Type one of, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `ma_child_is_in_continuous_eligibility_period`, `ma_is_adult_category`, `ma_is_emergency_medicaid_only`, `ma_is_in_pregnancy_coverage_period`, `ma_magi_category`, `ma_meets_adult_group_community_engagement_condition`, `ma_meets_residency`, `ma_meets_some_category_demographics`.

```
if it is not the case that Medicaid: meets the residency requirement
  then ineligible_residency
else if Medicaid: child is in a continuous eligibility period
  then eligible
else if Medicaid: is in the pregnancy coverage period
  then eligible
else if all of the following are true:
    - Medicaid: is emergency Medicaid only
    - it is not the case that Medicaid: MAGI covered group is equal to none
  then emergency_only
else if all of the following are true:
    - Medicaid: MAGI covered group is equal to none
    - Medicaid: meets the Adults MAGI category
    - it is not the case that Medicaid: Adults group community engagement condition
  then ineligible_community_engagement
else if all of the following are true:
    - Medicaid: MAGI covered group is equal to none
    - Medicaid: meets a MAGI category's non-income requirements
  then ineligible_income
else if Medicaid: MAGI covered group is equal to none
  then ineligible_no_category
otherwise eligible
```

### CO-556 Medicaid: child continuous eligibility end month `@engine`

The last month of a child's continuous eligibility period under 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.3.Q.2 and 42 CFR 435.926(c) - 11 months after the period's start month (a 12-month period inclusive of its start month), anchored on the month ma_application_date falls in, or on continuous_eligibility_period_start_month when that fact states an earlier month (a period already open from a prior determination or redetermination).

Precision. 8.100.3.Q.2 begins the period 'on the first day of the month the application is received, or from the date all criteria are met'; this item anchors on [month_of, ma_application_date] (P10), not [det_month], per the phase-3 review's C-4(c) finding, falling back to that anchor only when continuous_eligibility_period_start_month (CO-094) is unknown (P4, 'otherwise'). The end month is 11, not 12, months after the start month: 42 CFR 435.926(c)(1) states the period's length as 12 months and (c)(2) begins it on the application/all-criteria-met date, so a period beginning in month M covers M through M+11 inclusive (twelve months total) and ends with M+11, not M+12 - the phase-3 review's C-4(b) finding. Vocabulary fix round (U-7): reads ma_continuous_eligibility_months (CO-196) with pattern P44 instead of a hard-coded count, so a change to the parameter changes the rule.

```

### CO-562 Medicaid: is fully eligible for MAGI Medical Assistance (not emergency-only) `@engine`

Whether the person is eligible for full-scope MAGI Medical Assistance benefits, as distinct from the emergency-only benefit 42 CFR 435.406(b) and 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.2 grant to a person who otherwise qualifies but fails citizenship - a Colorado resident, not excluded as a patient in an institution for mental diseases (§ 8.100.3.G.1.c), who qualifies under at least one MAGI covered group and either meets the citizenship and immigration status requirement (CO-509) or, in the Children's or Pregnant category (including a needy newborn), is a Cover All Coloradans person (§ 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.1.a, CO-1173).

Precision. Distinct from ma_magi_is_eligible (CO-553), which is true for both full and emergency-only coverage. This item is what 10 CCR 2505-3-120.1.B's "eligible to receive assistance under Title XIX" exclusion and 42 CFR 457.310(b)(2)(i)'s "found eligible or potentially eligible for Medicaid" mean for CHP+'s purposes, per the phase-3 review's C-10 finding - a person whose only Title XIX entitlement is emergency services has nothing CHP+ needs to defer to. Phase 7 fix round: Cover All Coloradans reaches only the MAGI Children and Pregnant categories (ix.1.a; S-2, OQ-214), so an undocumented postpartum or 19-year-old person in the Adult or Parent and Caretaker Relative category is not fully eligible; and § 8.100.3.G.1.c's IMD exclusion is applied (S-5, CO-1179). OQ-214 sweep: C.R.S. 25.5-2-104(2) makes a child under 19 who would be eligible for medical assistance but for immigration status eligible for state medical assistance with the same benefits, and C.R.S. 25.5-5-201(6)(a) makes a pregnant non-citizen who meets every other requirement eligible for medical assistance; neither is limited to the categories § 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.1.a-b lists, so a child or pregnant person in any MAGI category is fully eligible whatever their status. A postpartum person who was not covered while pregnant is reached only by the rule's ix.1 list (still OQ-214).

### CO-564 Medicaid: under the child age limit, or turns 19 this month `@engine`

Whether the person is under ma_magi_child_age_limit (19), or is exactly 19 and their 19th birthday fell within the determination month - the age condition 8.100.4.G.2.a states as "eligible ... through the end of the month in which they turn 19 years old," which 8.100.3.G.1.g.viii.1's Cover All Coloradans exception and 10 CCR 2505-3-110.1.B.5.p (CHP+) repeat in identical words.

Precision. Age (CO-300) is whole years completed as of the determination date, so a person is not yet 19 on the day of their 19th birthday's own month until the birthday itself, and is exactly 19 from the birthday through the rest of that month. `[=, age, ma_magi_child_age_limit]` combined with `[=, [month_of, date_of_birth], [month_of, [det_date]]]` therefore isolates precisely the window '19, and the birthday was this month' without needing a date-plus-N-years engine operator: before the birthday day in that month, age is still 18 and the first disjunct already covers it; from the birthday day through the end of that month, age is 19 and the birth month matches the determination month; the following month, the birth month no longer matches and the person is correctly excluded.

Type yes/no, scope person, program Medicaid.
Uses: `age`, `date_of_birth`, `ma_magi_child_age_limit`.

  - Age is less than MAGI household child age limit (19)
  - all of the following are true:
    - Age is equal to MAGI household child age limit (19)
    - the month containing Date of birth is equal to the month containing the Determination Date
```

```

### CO-605 Medicaid: SSI-related countable earned income `@engine`

This person's (and, if living together, their spouse's) combined gross earned income for the month, after the $65 earned income exclusion, the unused portion of the $20 general income exclusion carried over from unearned income, and the one-half remainder disregard of 20 CFR 416.1112(c), 416.1124(c)(12) and 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.5.H.4.b.

Precision. Combines wages_gross across ma_ssi_household_size's spouse-living-together group (8.100.5.H.1.a's "mutually available" rule) before applying one $65 exclusion, plus any part of the combined group's $20 general exclusion not already used against unearned income (20 CFR 416.1124(c)(12), "If you have less than $20 of unearned income in a month and you have earned income in that month, we will use the rest of the $20 exclusion to reduce the amount of your countable earned income"), and one one-half disregard, to the combined total. The unearned-income sum recomputed here to find the unused $20 is the same group sum ma_ssi_countable_unearned_income (CO-606) uses. The Ineligible Child Allocation is deducted first, from an ineligible spouse's unearned income and then from that spouse's earned income (ma_ssi_child_allocation_from_spouse_earned, CO-2279), and the unused $20 is measured on the unearned income after that allocation (ma_ssi_household_unearned_income_counted, CO-2281; OQ-83). Deeming of a parent's income to an applicant child, and so the Ineligible Parent(s) Allocation, is not modeled (OQ-83). Vocabulary fix round (R-1): earned income includes net earnings from self-employment (ma_self_employment_net_earnings, CO-1704), which 8.100.5's earned income list names; it had read wages only. Vocabulary fix round (docs/reviews/vocabulary-reuse.md, R-8): reads resides_in_medical_institution (CO-1742), not SNAP's majority-of-meals institution fact.

Type money, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `ma_self_employment_net_earnings`, `ma_ssi_child_allocation_from_spouse_earned`, `ma_ssi_household_unearned_income_counted`, `relationships`, `resides_in_medical_institution`, `ssi_earned_income_disregard_rate`, `ssi_earned_income_exclusion`, `ssi_general_income_exclusion`, `wages_gross`.

```
(the greater of 0 and ((the sum of that person's Gross wages plus that person's Medicaid: net earnings from self-employment (non-MAGI) for each person in the persons joined to this person by spouse, crossing an edge only where (all of the following are true:;   - it is not the case that Resides in a medical institution;   - it is not the case that that person's Resides in a medical institution)) minus Medicaid: ineligible child allocation taken from an ineligible spouse's earned income) minus (SSI-related earned income exclusion (65) plus (the greater of 0 and SSI-related general income exclusion (20) minus Medicaid: SSI-related unearned income after allocations))) times SSI-related earned income disregard rate (0.5)
```

Phase 7 fix round (S-3): an Old Age Pension recipient who meets SSI criteria except the level of income (§ 8.100.6.K.4, SISC B; ma_oap_sisc_b_eligible, CO-1177) is reported oap_sisc_b when not otherwise SSI-related eligible.

### CO-617 Medicaid: Medicare Savings Program category `@engine`

The single Medicare Savings Program category this person qualifies under for the month, tested in the order Colorado's tiers of Medicare cost-sharing assistance run (10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.6.L-8.100.6.O) - QMB first (the most generous), then SLMB, then QI-1, then QDWI, or none.

Precision. QMB and SLMB/QI-1 are structured as increasing income bands that cannot overlap by construction (ma_slmb_eligible and ma_qi_eligible each exclude the tier below); QDWI is a separate track (Part A entitlement on a disability basis that has been or is being lost) that can coincide with none of the others, so testing it last is a matter of the category list's order, not exclusivity.

  then slmb
else if Medicaid: is Qualifying Individual 1 (QI-1) eligible
  then qi
else if Medicaid: is Qualified Disabled and Working Individual (QDWI) eligible
  then qdwi
otherwise none
```

### CO-646 Medicaid: Community Spouse Resource Allowance (CSRA) `@engine`

The amount of the couple's resources protected for the community spouse - the largest of (a) the couple's total resources at the § 8.100.7.L snapshot, but no more than the current CSRA maximum standard, (b) the increased CSRA of § 8.100.7.S (ma_csra_increased), and (c) an amount a court has ordered the institutionalized spouse to transfer to the community spouse - per 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.7.M.1.

Precision. OQ-126 resolved: § 8.100.7.M.1 takes the largest of three amounts; (b) and (c) were added in the open-question sweep. Branch (a) gives the community spouse the couple's total resources up to the maximum, which 42 U.S.C. 1396r-5(f)(2)(A)(i) permits as a State plan standard set at the maximum (S1222): the spousal-share and minimum-standard terms never bind for such a State. § 8.100.7.M.1.a has no spousal-share (half-of-total) term and no minimum-standard floor; that shape belongs to 42 U.S.C. 1396r-5(f)(2)(A) (S371), which Colorado's fetched text does not adopt - see OQ-126. ma_csra_minimum (CO-827) is accordingly not read here. Reads ma_spousal_resources_at_snapshot (CO-888), not ssi_countable_resources_couple (CO-801), per the phase-4 review's C-13 finding: § 8.100.7.L's resource assessment is taken "at the time of initial Medical Assistance application" and § 8.100.7.M.1 says the CSRA is "established at intake only," while CO-801 is the current-month figure § 8.100.7.O.1 tests against the CSRA each month (CO-647) - the two must be able to differ once the couple spends down.

### CO-649 Medicaid: transfer penalty period, whole months `@engine`

The number of whole months this person is ineligible for Long-Term Care services because of an uncompensated transfer of assets within the 60-month look-back period - the uncompensated value divided by the average regional monthly private-pay rate, with any partial month reported separately - per 42 U.S.C. 1396p(c)(1)(E) and 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.7.F.2.c.i-d. Zero if the transfer was exempt.

Precision. A whole number, the floor of the division in § 8.100.7.F.2.c.i; the remaining partial month is § 8.100.7.F.2.d's separate day calculation (thirty days times the decimal fractional share, rounded up), reported by ma_transfer_penalty_days (CO-659) rather than folded into this item as a fraction of a month, per the phase-4 review's C-6 finding. The start date (8.100.7.F.2.c.ii) is transfer_penalty_period_start_date (CO-886), which ma_transfer_penalty_applies (CO-660) reads. Between institutionalized spouses (8.100.7.F.8) the division is multiplied by this person's share (ma_transfer_penalty_share_rate, CO-2235: half when apportioned) before the floor, and the months reassigned from a spouse who died or left the institution (ma_transfer_penalty_months_assigned_from_spouse, CO-2233) are added (OQ-94, resolved). Expressed as the negation of ceil(-x) because the pattern catalog has no floor operator.

Type whole number, scope person, program Medicaid.

if Transfer was exempt
  then 0
otherwise (-1 times (-1 times (Medicaid: share of the transfer penalty this person serves times (Uncompensated transfer value in look-back divided by Transfer penalty divisor (10814.64))) rounded up to the next whole dollar)) plus Transfer penalty months assigned from the spouse
```

The single Long-Term Care eligibility outcome for this person for the month - eligible for institutional, HCBS, or PACE services, or the reason for ineligibility - per 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.7.

Precision. A Cover All Coloradans person who reaches the setting branches but fits neither HCBS nor, lacking status, institutional care or PACE is ineligible_status; a status-meeting institutionalized person without nursing facility level of care is ineligible_level_of_care; anyone else left (a waiver designee outside the waiver's age criteria, for example) is not_institutionalized_or_waiver, in place of the former misleading ineligible_income default. ### CO-653 Medicaid: is HCBS waiver eligible `@engine`

Whether this person is eligible for a Home and Community-Based Services waiver for the month - a Colorado resident who is aged, blind or disabled, meets the citizenship and immigration status requirement (or, as a child, pregnant or postpartum person, Cover All Coloradans), is designated for a waiver's target group within its age criteria, meets the level of care that waiver requires, and is eligible through the special income group, SSI eligibility, or the Working Adults with Disabilities Buy-In (for the EBD, CMHS, BI, CIH, SLS and DD waivers) - per 10 CCR 2505-10 §§ 8.100.3.F.1.g, 8.100.3.G.1, 8.100.7.B.1, 8.7100.C and 8.7100.D.

Precision. Phase 7 - the designated waiver's age criteria (ma_hcbs_waiver_age_criteria_met, CO-1164, § 8.7101) are tested, and the Buy-In waiver list names the Complementary and Integrative Health waiver (CIH), the current name of the former Spinal Cord Injury waiver, as § 8.7101.H and its eligibility-group list state. § 8.100.7.B.1.c's Buy-In route is not gated on ma_ltc_financially_eligible (which requires the special income group and the LTC resource standard) because § 8.100.6.P.1.c states Buy-In resources are not counted and its income test is 450% FPL, not 300% of the SSI benefit rate; it is limited instead to the waivers § 8.100.7.B.1.c.i names. Phase 7 fix round: residency, aged/blind/disabled (§ 8.100.3.F.1.g) and status are tested (B-3), status through ma_meets_status_for_cover_all_coloradans_categories (CO-1174) because § 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.1.b reaches the Long-Term Care waivers except PACE; and the level of care is the designated waiver's (ma_meets_designated_waiver_level_of_care, CO-1178: ICF/IID for CES, SLS, DD and CHRP's developmental disability route, nursing facility or hospital for CwCHN and CIH), not nursing facility level of care for every waiver (S-4, D-75 § 8.7101). The SSI-related route is open to every waiver although § 8.7101.C.3 lists CHRP's served groups as foster care children and 42 CFR 435.217 only (N-4); CHRP's population is children, for whom the special income group route gives the same result. Needs-fact sweep: the designated waiver's diagnoses, settings and BI's injury before 65 are tested (ma_meets_hcbs_waiver_condition_criteria, CO-2270; OQ-210, resolved). A person in a Medicaid Buy-In program has no spousal impoverishment computation (ma_ltc_couple, CO-643; OQ-127, resolved).

Uses: `ma_transfer_penalty_months`, `ma_transfer_penalty_months_assigned_from_spouse`, `ma_transfer_penalty_share_rate`, `transfer_penalty_divisor`, `transfer_was_exempt`, `uncompensated_transfer_value_in_lookback`.

```
if Transfer was exempt
  then 0
otherwise 30 times ((Medicaid: share of the transfer penalty this person serves times (Uncompensated transfer value in look-back divided by Transfer penalty divisor (10814.64))) minus (Medicaid: transfer penalty period, whole months minus Transfer penalty months assigned from the spouse)) rounded up to the next whole dollar
```

```

### CO-662 Medicaid: MMMNA standard `@engine`

The current minimum monthly maintenance needs allowance before any excess shelter allowance - 150% of the federal poverty level for a family of two, per 42 U.S.C. 1396r-5(d)(3)(A)(i)/(B)(iii) and 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.7.Q.1.a.

Precision. § 8.100.7.Q.1.a (S358) states the MMMNA 'is equal to 150% of the federal poverty level for a family of two and is adjusted in July of each year'; federal_poverty_guideline_annual_table (CO-181) already carries the size-2 annual guideline this batch needs, so the standard is derived - ma_mmmna_applicable_pct (CO-1801) times one-twelfth of the size-2 guideline - rather than supplied as its own annually-invented figure, per the phase-4 review's G-1 finding. OQ-145 resolved: the size-2 guideline is read from ma_mmmna_poverty_guideline_family_of_two_annual (CO-1954), dated from each July 1, so January through June uses the guideline adjusted the previous July ($2,643.75 for January-June 2026, from the 2025 guideline) and July 2026 on uses $2,705.00, the figure CMS publishes (D-72).

### CO-704 CHP+: household income is within the CHP+ limit `@engine`

Whether this person's chp_household_income, as a percentage of the poverty guideline, falls within the band 10 CCR 2505-3-110.1.E states for a child (greater than 142%, not exceeding 260% of FPL) or 110.1.F states for a pregnant woman (greater than 195%, not exceeding 260% of FPL), applying the 42 CFR 435.603(d)(4)/10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.4.D 5% disregard only when it makes the difference for CHP+, the highest MAGI income standard a child or pregnant person in this band could qualify under.

Precision. The 5% disregard (ma_magi_income_disregard_pct) is tested as an alternative to the plain ratio, not always subtracted, because subtracting it unconditionally could push a household that already qualifies without it below the lower bound (a household at 142.5% of FPL, for example, would fail the 142% floor once 5 points are subtracted, which is not what the disregard is for). This item is therefore true when either the plain ma_magi_household_income_pct_fpl falls in the band, or the ratio less the disregard does; both compare against the same lower/upper parameters for the person's category (child or pregnant).

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program CHP+.
Uses: `chp_income_limit_pct_upper`, `is_pregnant`, `ma_income_limit_child_pct`, `ma_income_limit_pregnant_pct`, `ma_is_under_child_age_or_turns_nineteen_this_month`, `ma_magi_household_income_pct_fpl`, `ma_magi_income_disregard_pct`.

Precision. Citizenship/immigration status (110.1.B) reads ma_meets_status_for_cover_all_coloradans_categories (CO-1174: the Medicaid status test, CO-509, or the Cover All Coloradans population, CO-1173) rather than restating 110.1.B's own long list of specific immigration categories, because 110.1.B.5.o's Cover All Coloradans exception reaches every person under 19 regardless of status (phase 7 fix round: CO-509 no longer carries that exception itself, S-2); for CHP+'s population (children and pregnant women only), the two tests are equivalent in outcome even though 110.1.B's list and 8.100.3.G.1.g's list are not worded identically. 10 CCR 2505-3-120.1.C's exclusion of an inmate of a public institution or a patient in an institution for mental diseases reads is_inmate_of_public_institution (CO-1105) and is_patient_in_institution_for_mental_diseases (CO-1104), added in phase 7 (OQ-58, resolved), not snap_resides_in_institution_providing_meals, which means a nursing-facility or similar long-term care admission; the 90-days-before-release reentry services § 120.1.C carves out are a benefit, not eligibility, and are not modeled. ### CO-707 CHP+: eligibility status `@engine`

The single CHP+ eligibility outcome for the month - eligible as a child, eligible as a pregnant (prenatal) applicant, or one of six specific ineligibility reasons (Medicaid-eligible instead per 10 CCR 2505-3-120.1.B, income outside the CHP+ band per 110.1.E-F, other creditable coverage per 120.1.A, failing residency per 110.1.D, failing citizenship/immigration status per 110.1.B, or an inmate of a public institution or a patient in an institution for mental diseases per 120.1.C), or ineligible for a reason this batch does not distinguish further (for example not a child and not pregnant).

Precision. Evaluated in the order the branches are listed - eligible outcomes first, then the specific ineligibility reasons. Fix round (C-14): residency and citizenship/status are checked immediately after the eligible and Medicaid-eligible branches and before the income and coverage tests, so a child or pregnant applicant who fails residency or citizenship is reported ineligible_residency or ineligible_status rather than falling through to the income catch-all - Phase 7 (OQ-58): a child or pregnant applicant who passes every other test, including income, but is an inmate of a public institution or a patient in an institution for mental diseases (10 CCR 2505-3 § 120.1.C) is reported ineligible_institution; income is tested explicitly before it so an income failure keeps its own reason - matching this volume's ma_magi_eligibility_status (CO-554) convention of checking residency before income, and correcting the prior ordering, which the phase-3 review's C-14 finding found reported every residency or citizenship failure as ineligible_income regardless of the actual reason.

Type one of, scope person-month, program CHP+.
Uses: `chp_child_is_eligible`, `chp_has_other_health_coverage`, `chp_income_within_limit`, `chp_prenatal_is_eligible`, `is_colorado_resident`, `is_pregnant`, `ma_is_under_child_age_or_turns_nineteen_this_month`, `ma_magi_is_fully_eligible`, `ma_meets_status_for_cover_all_coloradans_categories`.

else if all of the following are true:

  then ineligible_medicaid_eligible
else if all of the following are true:

else if all of the following are true:

### CO-1217 Home Care Allowance: eligibility status `@engine`

The person's Home Care Allowance eligibility for the month, checked in order - age five or older, Colorado residency, living in a home rather than a facility, not receiving and not functionally eligible for HCBS, an HCA tier, then the financial routes - eligible only if every check passes, per 9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.61.B, 3.570.11.A, 3.570.12 ("Home"), 3.570.13 and 3.570.14.D.

Precision. '"Home" (3.570.12) is a non-facility residence and "cannot include a homeless shelter or other temporary setting"; this item reads snap_resides_in_institution_providing_meals for a facility stay and is_homeless (CO-037) for a shelter (phase-8 fix round, S-5); another temporary setting is af_resides_in_temporary_setting (CO-2010). Functional eligibility for HCBS bars HCA at application and at reassessment, except during the stay of up to three months while a transition delayed outside the client's control is completed (3.570.11.A.2.b, af_hca_is_in_hcbs_transition_period, CO-2009); both facts are read as false when a case does not state them.' Vocabulary fix round (docs/reviews/vocabulary-reuse.md, R-8): reads resides_in_medical_institution (CO-1742), not SNAP's majority-of-meals institution fact.

Type one of, scope person-month, program AdultFinancial.
Uses: `af_hca_financially_eligible`, `af_hca_functionally_eligible_for_hcbs`, `af_hca_is_in_hcbs_transition_period`, `af_hca_min_age`, `af_hca_tier`, `af_meets_residency`, `af_resides_in_temporary_setting`, `age`, `is_homeless`, `receives_hcbs_services`, `resides_in_medical_institution`.

```
if Age is less than Home Care Allowance minimum age (5)
  then ineligible_age
else if it is not the case that Adult Financial: meets residency requirement
  then ineligible_residency
else if any of the following is true:
    - Resides in a medical institution
    - Is homeless
    - Home Care Allowance: lives in a temporary setting, otherwise no
  then ineligible_setting
else if any of the following is true:
    - Receives Home and Community Based Services
    - all of the following are true:
      - Home Care Allowance: functionally eligible for HCBS
      - it is not the case that Home Care Allowance: within the transition to HCBS after reassessment, otherwise no
  then ineligible_hcbs
else if Home Care Allowance: tier is equal to none
  then ineligible_functional
else if it is not the case that Home Care Allowance: financially eligible
  then ineligible_financial
otherwise eligible

### CO-1270 Colorado Works: eligible for a diversion payment `@engine`

Whether the person's assistance unit may receive a Colorado Works diversion payment for the month - it is eligible for basic cash assistance, or fails only the basic cash assistance income test and is within the county's higher diversion income limit; the assessment finds it does not need long-term or basic cash assistance; it demonstrates a specific crisis need under a diversion agreement; and it is not within an earlier diversion's period of ineligibility - per 9 CCR 2503-6 3.601 ("Diversion") and 3.606.8.A.

Precision. The rule has a single diversion program with a county income option (3.606.8.A.6), which relaxes only the income test (phase-8 fix round, S-1): a unit ineligible for any other reason (no dependent child, residency, status, living arrangement, time limit, sanction closure) is not diversion-eligible whatever the county limit; it states no separate state and county diversion programs. A client cannot receive diversion in a month it receives basic cash assistance (A.7); the unit that needs no basic cash assistance does not take it, so the conjunct needs_long_term_cash_assistance = false covers it. The payment amount is needs-based and not modeled; the period of ineligibility cannot exceed the maximum grant for the household size over the same period (A.4), which is the county's computation. Diversion payments do not count toward the time limit (A.6).

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program ColoradoWorks.
Uses: `cw_eligibility_status`, `has_specific_crisis_need`, `in_diversion_period_of_ineligibility`, `meets_county_diversion_income_limit`, `needs_long_term_cash_assistance`.

all of the following are true:
  - any of the following is true:
    - Colorado Works: eligibility status is equal to eligible
    - all of the following are true:
      - Colorado Works: eligibility status is equal to ineligible_income
      - Meets the county's diversion income limit
  - it is not the case that Needs long-term or basic cash assistance
  - Has a specific crisis need
  - it is not the case that In a diversion period of ineligibility
```

["all",["any",["=","cw_eligibility_status","eligible"],["all",["=","cw_eligibility_status","ineligible_income"],"meets_county_diversion_income_limit"]],["not","needs_long_term_cash_assistance"],"has_specific_crisis_need",["not","in_diversion_period_of_ineligibility"]]
```

### CO-1508 Colorado Works: death reimbursement amount `@engine`

The Colorado Works death reimbursement benefit for a deceased client - for a client who received Colorado Works while alive, when the total combined charges for the disposition (a prepaid plot of $2,000 or less, or a donated one, not counted) are at most $2,500 - the lesser of the $1,500 maximum and the charges the decedent's estate leaves unpaid, reduced by the insurance proceeds and by the legally responsible persons' resources over the SSI limit, never below zero; zero otherwise. Per 9 CCR 2503-6 3.606.7.A.2, B, E and F.1-2.

Precision. Insurance proceeds (F.2.f, 'used to reduce the maximum Death Reimbursement') and the responsible persons' resources over the SSI limit (F.2.c, 'used to reduce the State Department funded Death Reimbursement payment') reduce the payment; the estate (B.2, F.2.b) reduces the charges the payment can cover. The Adult Financial burial benefit applies all three against the full costs (3.570.43.D); the two orders give different amounts when the charges are well under $1,500 or the offsets are large (OQ-354). The responsible persons' excess resources are read from af_burial_responsible_person_excess_resources (CO-1229), the same SSI-limit computation 3.606.7.F.2.c states, cross-program rather than duplicated. Voluntary contributions from the responsible party (F.2.c) are not modeled; contributions from non-responsible parties do not reduce the benefit (F.2.g). A Social Security lump-sum death benefit is not counted (F.2.e), as burial_responsible_person_resources (CO-1225) already states.

Type money, scope person, program ColoradoWorks.
Uses: `af_burial_responsible_person_excess_resources`, `burial_insurance_proceeds`, `burial_plot_cost_excluded_from_limit`, `burial_services_total_cost`, `cw_death_reimbursement_cost_limit`, `cw_death_reimbursement_max`, `decedent_estate_value`, `is_deceased_colorado_works_client`.

```
if all of the following are true:
    - Deceased Colorado Works client
    - (Total cost of burial services minus Burial plot cost excluded from the burial cost limit) is at most Colorado Works death reimbursement total charge limit (2500)
  then the greater of 0 and ((the lesser of Colorado Works death reimbursement maximum (1500) and Total cost of burial services minus Decedent's available estate) minus Burial insurance proceeds) minus Burial assistance: legally responsible person's resources over the SSI limit
otherwise 0
```

["case",[["all","is_deceased_colorado_works_client",["<=",["-","burial_services_total_cost","burial_plot_cost_excluded_from_limit"],"cw_death_reimbursement_cost_limit"]],["max",0,["-",["-",["min","cw_death_reimbursement_max",["-","burial_services_total_cost","decedent_estate_value"]],"burial_insurance_proceeds"],"af_burial_responsible_person_excess_resources"]]],["else",0]]

### CO-1511 Adult Financial: barred by Colorado Works `@engine`

Whether the person is barred from Adult Financial programs for the month because of Colorado Works - currently receiving Colorado Works financial assistance, eligible for it, or in a Colorado Works case closed for a sanction - per 9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.61.F and 3.520.71.F.2.

Precision. Receipt is read from receives_tanf_cash (CO-013); eligibility and the sanction closure from the person's own cw_eligibility_status (CO-921) - eligible, or sanction_closure (a fourth-level sanction, 3.608.4.C.2). A specified caretaker who is not a parent is not required to join the Colorado Works case (3.520.71.F.1.a); such a person is not in a Colorado Works assistance unit in this volume (CO-900 joins parents and caretakers to their own dependent children only), so cw_eligibility_status does not report them eligible. A closure for demonstrable evidence or a disqualification, or a withdrawal before benefits are exhausted, that still stands (F.2.a-c) is the supplied af_has_open_colorado_works_closure_bar (CO-2008), read as false when a case does not state it. The duty of F.1 to apply for Colorado Works is not a separate test: the bar reads Colorado Works eligibility directly (OQ-357).

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program AdultFinancial.
Uses: `af_has_open_colorado_works_closure_bar`, `cw_eligibility_status`, `receives_tanf_cash`.

```
any of the following is true:
  - Receives TANF cash assistance
  - Colorado Works: eligibility status is one of: eligible, sanction_closure
  - Adult Financial: Colorado Works case closed for demonstrable evidence, disqualification or withdrawal, otherwise no
```

["any","receives_tanf_cash",["in","cw_eligibility_status",["eligible","sanction_closure"]],["otherwise","af_has_open_colorado_works_closure_bar",false]]
```

Precision. Only the client without an SSN or proof of application is ineligible, not the unit (3.604.3.B.2.c, K). At application a furnished number or proof of an application satisfies it (ssn_is_verified); at a redetermination the number itself must have been verified (ssn_verified_by_electronic_data_source), since a client who applied for an SSN at the initial determination must have it verified before the next recertification (3.604.3.B.2.c.1, S1630; phase-10 sweep, OQ-373). ### CO-2000 Colorado Works: needs deducted in minor-parent deeming `@engine`

For an unmarried minor parent, the needs deducted from her non-participant parents' countable income before it is deemed to her assistance unit under 9 CCR 2503-6 3.605.1.A.4.a: the needs of the parent or parents living in the home and of the individuals in the home for whom they are responsible, measured as the Colorado Works need standard for a unit of those parents and the parents' other children in the home - the One Caretaker row for one parent, the Two Caretakers row for two, keyed by the number of other children.

Precision. The parents are the persons of whom this person is a child (a stated parent edge, read as living in the home, as cw_deemed_parent_income_of_minor_parent, CO-909, reads it). The individuals the parents are responsible for are this person's siblings and half siblings in the case (P43, shared parent), excluding this person herself, whose needs her own assistance unit meets; her own child is not her parent's child. No sibling is a member of the minor parent's assistance unit under cw_assistance_unit_members (CO-900), which does not cross the edge to her parent, so none is excluded on that ground. A stepparent of the minor parent, or another person a parent supports, is not counted. Above ten children the chart's each-additional amount is added.

Type money, scope person, program ColoradoWorks.
Uses: `cw_need_standard_each_additional`, `cw_need_standard_table`, `cw_need_standard_table_two_caretakers`, `relationships`.

```
if (the number of persons in all persons in every person in the case such that this person is a child of that person) is at least 2
  then (if (the number of persons in the persons who share a parent with this person) is at most 10;   then Colorado Works need standard by number of children (two caretakers) (table), for the number of persons in the persons who share a parent with this person; otherwise Colorado Works need standard by number of children (two caretakers) (table), for 10 plus (Colorado Works need standard, each additional child (one caretaker) (67) times ((the number of persons in the persons who share a parent with this person) minus 10)))
otherwise (if (the number of persons in the persons who share a parent with this person) is at most 10;   then Colorado Works need standard by number of children (one caretaker) (table), for the number of persons in the persons who share a parent with this person; otherwise Colorado Works need standard by number of children (one caretaker) (table), for 10 plus (Colorado Works need standard, each additional child (one caretaker) (67) times ((the number of persons in the persons who share a parent with this person) minus 10)))
```

```json
["case",[[">=",["count",["filter",["persons"],["rel",["child"],["P"]]]],2],["case",[["<=",["count",["shared_relative","parent"]],10],["lookup","cw_need_standard_table_two_caretakers",["count",["shared_relative","parent"]]]],["else",["+",["lookup","cw_need_standard_table_two_caretakers",10],["*","cw_need_standard_each_additional",["-",["count",["shared_relative","parent"]],10]]]]]],["else",["case",[["<=",["count",["shared_relative","parent"]],10],["lookup","cw_need_standard_table",["count",["shared_relative","parent"]]]],["else",["+",["lookup","cw_need_standard_table",10],["*","cw_need_standard_each_additional",["-",["count",["shared_relative","parent"]],10]]]]]]]
```

### CO-2352 Colorado Works: budgetary unit members `@engine`

The persons in this person's Colorado Works budgetary unit who live in the home: every member of the assistance unit (an optional member who requested assistance included), and the spouse of a parent or non-parent caretaker in the assistance unit whether or not the spouse requested assistance, unless the spouse receives SSI or a Title IV payment (9 CCR 2503-6 3.604.2.D).

Precision. The other members of D.1 enter the income test by their own items: the non-recipient parents of a minor parent (D.1.d) through cw_deemed_parent_income_of_minor_parent (CO-909), and the sponsor of a non-citizen (D.1.e) through cw_sponsor_deemed_income (CO-2365), since the sponsor does not live in the home. The unborn child of a pregnant parent (D.1.c) has no income, and the standards of 3.606.1.F count the assistance unit ("based upon those included in the assistance unit"); the pregnancy allowance carries the pregnancy (3.606.1.G).

### CO-900 Colorado Works: assistance unit members `@engine`

The persons who make up this person's Colorado Works assistance unit under 9 CCR 2503-6 3.604.2.A-C and 26-2-703(2.5), C.R.S. - a dependent child living with a caretaker, and that caretaker (the child's parent, or a non-parent caretaker who requests assistance), crossed reciprocally, with the spouse of a pregnant parent and, when they request assistance, a stepparent, a non-parent caretaker's spouse and the other optional members of 3.604.2.C.2, except that the edge between a dependent child who is themselves a minor parent and that minor parent's own parent is not crossed, because 3.604.2.C.1.b excludes a minor parent's own parent from mandatory inclusion when the minor parent is requesting assistance for their own child. Excludes anyone receiving SSI or a Title IV foster care, adoption subsidy, or kinship payment (3.604.2.C.3) and an optional member who has not requested assistance (C.2). Each member's value of this item is the same set (their own unit); an excluded person's own value is empty or a singleton of themselves.

Precision. As with snap_household_members (CO-305) and ma_magi_household_members (CO-500), a stated parent/child relationship edge is read as 'living in the home' - this volume does not model the 3.604.2.E-G temporary-absence exceptions or the 3.604.2.H multiple-caretaker hierarchy. Phase-10 sweep (OQ-152, OQ-101): a spouse edge is crossed when either spouse is a parent or caretaker of a dependent child in the home or is pregnant, so the spouse of a pregnant parent (C.1.e, mandatory), a stepparent (C.2.a) and a non-parent caretaker's spouse (C.2.c) are reached; the edge between a minor parent requesting assistance for her own child and her parent is crossed when that parent requests inclusion (C.2.g); and the final filter leaves out cw_is_excluded_from_assistance_unit (CO-2350): SSI and Title IV recipients (C.3) and an optional member (cw_is_optional_assistance_unit_member, CO-2349) who has not requested assistance. Siblings and half siblings are reached through their parent or caretaker as dependent children (C.1.c-d); those made optional by custody or child support (C.2.d-f) are stated by cw_is_optional_member_by_custody_or_support (CO-2347). A pregnancy left unstated is read as none for the spouse edge.

Per 3.605.1.A.4.a's formula: each such parent's gross earned income minus the $90 employment disregard (floored at zero), plus their unearned income, summed over the parents in the home, minus the needs of those parents and of the individuals in the home for whom they are responsible (cw_minor_parent_deeming_needs_deduction, CO-2000: the need standard for the parents and their other children; OQ-102). Open-question sweep: the deduction had been the One Caretaker need standard for zero children, deducted once per parent; it now counts the parents' other children (3.605.1.A.4.a, S1307) and is deducted once from the parents' combined income. Does not deduct maintenance or child support the parent pays outside the home, or amounts paid to tax dependents outside the home (3.605.1.A.4.a's other two deductions) - not modeled this batch. Fix round (C-11(a)): the deeming guard now reads marital_status = single, per 3.605.1.A.4's own title and first sentence ('Income of a non-participant stepparent and a non-participant parent of an unmarried minor parent') - a married minor parent's own parent's income was previously deemed too, which the rule's own text excludes. Fix round (C-11(b)): reads [of, [P], cw_countable_unearned_income] (CO-908) for the parent's unearned income instead of re-enumerating four of its six components (social_security_income, pension_income, unemployment_income, other_unearned_income_nontaxable), which had silently dropped tanf_cash_income and child_support_received; 3.605.1.A.4.a's 'plus any unearned income' does not admit a shorter list than the program's own unearned-income definition. Vocabulary fix round (R-1): earned income is cw_gross_earned_income (CO-1716): gross wages plus the self-employment net profit 3.605.2.E.1.c treats as earned income; it had read wages only.

Phase 8 - less the sanction reduction of 9 CCR 2503-6 3.608.4.C (cw_sanction_reduction, CO-1265), with the cents dropped.

Precision. Drops cents by flooring rather than rounding (3.606.1.K.2's 'drop the cents'); the engine has a round-up (ceil) operator but no floor, so this item computes floor(x) as -ceil(-x), which is exact for any real x. The pre-sanction grant (cw_grant_before_sanction, CO-1260) subtracts cw_payment_countable_income (CO-923), computed with the payment disregards of the current 3.606.2.A (S1000) - 100% in the first certification period and for a new source, 67% for a current source after it (phase-8 fix round, B-1) - not cw_countable_income (CO-910), which carries the eligibility-test figure. The $10 pregnancy allowance (3.606.1.G) is added in CO-1260. Phase 8 (OQ-141 resolved): the sanction reduction of 3.608.4.C (cw_sanction_reduction, CO-1265) is subtracted here.

Type money, scope person-month, program ColoradoWorks.
Uses: `cw_grant_before_sanction`, `cw_sanction_reduction`.

```
the greater of 0 and -1 times (-1 times (Colorado Works: grant before any sanction minus Colorado Works: sanction reduction) rounded up to the next whole dollar)
```

["max",0,["*",-1,["ceil",["*",-1,["-","cw_grant_before_sanction","cw_sanction_reduction"]]]]]

### CO-915 Colorado Works: months of assistance used `@engine`

The number of months already counted toward this person's sixty-month federal TANF lifetime limit, per 26-2-706.5, C.R.S. and 9 CCR 2503-6 3.606.6.A and F - the statewide automated system's running count less the months received while living in exempt Indian Country, zeroed out for anyone who is not the head of the assistance unit or the head's spouse, per 45 CFR 264.1(b)(1)(i)'s bar on counting a non-head, non-spouse member's months toward the limit.

Precision. 45 CFR 264.1(b)(1)(i) (S421): 'States must not count toward the five-year limit: (i) Any month of receipt of assistance by an individual who is not the head-of-household or married to the head-of-household.' A dependent child's or a non-head adult's own months_of_assistance_received are therefore read as 0 here regardless of the supplied count, so cw_time_limit_reached (CO-918)'s unit-level test only ever sums a head-of-household's or spouse's months. Vocabulary fix round (R-3, R-7): the head is the Colorado Works head of the assistance unit (cw_is_head_of_assistance_unit, CO-1733), not the SNAP head of household; and 3.606.6.F's Indian Country months are subtracted (cw_months_received_in_exempt_indian_country, CO-1723) instead of zeroing every month for a tribal member. Phase-10 sweep (OQ-143): 9 CCR 2503-6 3.604.2.M (S1004) counts the month of a disqualified or ineligible member (cw_is_disqualified_member, CO-928) toward that member's own sixty-month maximum when a grant is paid for others in the unit, so such a member's count is read as stated even when the member is neither the head nor the head's spouse; Colorado's rule counts more than 45 CFR 264.1(b)(1)(i) requires, and the volume follows the rule.

Type whole number, scope person, program ColoradoWorks.
Uses: `cw_is_disqualified_member`, `cw_is_head_of_assistance_unit`, `cw_months_received_in_exempt_indian_country`, `months_of_assistance_received`, `relationships`.

```
if any of the following is true:
    - Colorado Works: is head of the assistance unit
    - there is a person of whom this person is a spouse such that
      that person's Colorado Works: is head of the assistance unit
    - Colorado Works: is a disqualified or ineligible member
  then the greater of 0 and Months of federal TANF assistance received minus Colorado Works: months of assistance received while living in exempt Indian Country
otherwise 0
```

["case",[["any","cw_is_head_of_assistance_unit",["exists_related",["spouse"],["of",["P"],"cw_is_head_of_assistance_unit"]],"cw_is_disqualified_member"],["max",0,["-","months_of_assistance_received","cw_months_received_in_exempt_indian_country"]]],["else",0]]

### CO-918 Colorado Works: time limit reached `@engine`

This person's assistance unit contains an adult (or minor head-of-household) member who has used sixty or more cumulative months of federal TANF assistance, and the unit is not exempt from (or extended beyond) the time limit - per 9 CCR 2503-6 3.606.6.C ("an assistance unit containing an individual who has received ... assistance ... as an adult for sixty (60) or more cumulative months shall not be eligible") and 45 CFR 264.1(a)(1). Every member of the same unit shares the same value.

Precision. Read at the unit level per the phase-5 review's C-2 finding: 3.606.6.C bars the whole unit, not only the member whose own count reached sixty months, so a unit containing one adult past the limit is time-limit-reached for every member, including a dependent child or a caretaker whose own months are under sixty. Tests cw_is_adult_member (CO-924) so a dependent child's own (zero) months never trigger the unit-level test directly, though cw_months_of_assistance_used (CO-915) already zeroes a non-head, non-spouse member's count.

Type yes/no, scope person, program ColoradoWorks.
Uses: `cw_assistance_unit_members`, `cw_is_adult_member`, `cw_months_of_assistance_used`, `cw_time_limit_months`, `cw_unit_time_limit_extended`.

```
all of the following are true:
  - there is a person in Colorado Works: assistance unit members such that
    all of the following are true:
      - that person's Colorado Works: is an adult member for the time limit
      - that person's Colorado Works: months of assistance used is at least Colorado Works lifetime time limit (60)
  - it is not the case that Colorado Works: unit time limit extended or exempt
```

### CO-919 Colorado Works: is a work-eligible individual `@engine`

The person is a "work-eligible individual" under 45 CFR 261.2(n) - an adult (or minor child head-of-household) receiving Colorado Works assistance, or a non-recipient parent living with a child receiving it - unless the person is a minor parent who is not the head of household, a non-citizen ineligible for assistance due to immigration status, or an SSI recipient (Colorado's state-option exclusion, read as elected because it tracks the same SSI exclusion 3.604.2.C.3.a states for assistance unit membership).

Precision. Fix round (C-6): three defects the phase-5 review found. (a) No assistance test at all: added the last conjunct below, reading cw_eligibility_status (CO-921) directly rather than a bare literal-18 age test - this person's own unit is eligible, or this person is a non-recipient parent living with a child whose own unit is eligible (261.2(n)(1)'s 'non-recipient parent living with a child receiving such assistance'). No circularity with CO-921, which does not read this item. (b) The prior second conjunct, [not, [all, [<, age, 18], [not, snap_is_head_of_household]]], was by De Morgan's law identical to the first conjunct and never read cw_has_dependent_child, so it excluded every non-head minor rather than 261.2(n)(1)(i)'s minor-parent-who-is-not-head-of-household; rewritten below to read cw_has_dependent_child. (c) The bare literal 18 in the first conjunct is replaced with cw_dependent_child_age_limit (CO-270), per governance's name.digits rule, since 261.2(n)'s 'adult' is the complement of the minor child the same title defines. Scope changed from person to person-month because the new assistance-test conjunct reads cw_eligibility_status (CO-921), which is person-month. Vocabulary fix round (R-7): reads cw_is_head_of_assistance_unit (CO-1733), not the SNAP head of household.

### CO-921 Colorado Works: eligibility status `@engine`

This person's Colorado Works eligibility determination for the month, checked in order - no dependent child in the unit, residency, citizenship/immigrant status, a minor parent's living arrangement, the sixty-month time limit, then the income test - eligible only if every check passes. Phase 8 - a unit serving a fourth-level sanction is closed for the month (3.608.4.C.2), reported as sanction_closure after the time-limit check.

Precision. ineligible_resources is never reached by this item's derivation: 26-2-706(2)(a) expressly forbids an asset test as a condition of Colorado Works eligibility, so this volume does not author cw_countable_resources or cw_meets_resource_limit items. The option is kept in the fixed vocabulary for schema compatibility with the batch-10 interface; see the batch report. Fix round (C-13): adds a branch gated on cw_minor_parent_living_arrangement_met (CO-906), which no item previously read, per 26-2-706(2)(b) ('an unmarried parent under eighteen years of age shall not receive assistance unless' the stated living-arrangement conditions are met) and 3.604.2.N.1 ('grant payments may not be approved unless the minor parent resides with another adult caretaker or ... an appropriate setting'). CO-906's own vacuous-true design (satisfied whenever the person is not both under 18 and a parent) means this branch is a no-op for anyone who is not an unmarried minor parent.

### CO-922 Colorado Works: payment countable earned income `@engine`

This person's gross earned income for the month less the earned income disregard that determines the payment amount, floored at zero, per 9 CCR 2503-6 3.606.2.A - one hundred percent (nothing counts) at application and through the unit's first certification period (A.1) or for a new source of earned income in the first certification period that the income impacts (A.2.a); sixty-seven percent for a current source after the first certification period (A.1, last sentence; A.2.b). The figure the grant payment is computed from; distinct from the $90 eligibility test at application, which cw_countable_earned_income (CO-907) carries.

Precision. Applies the disregard to every person's own earned income, the same assumption cw_countable_earned_income (CO-907) states for the $90 disregard, since 3.606.2.A reads 'gross wages for clients' without an adult-only limitation. A unit not yet receiving (receives_tanf_cash false) is at application, whose payment A.1 computes with the 100% disregard for the first certification period. For a unit currently receiving, neither cw_in_first_certification_period (CO-1501) nor cw_is_new_earned_income_source (CO-1502) has a default: a case must state which situation a person's earnings fall in; a person with no earned income needs neither, since nothing is disregarded from zero. A person whose month mixes a new and a current source states the new part as cw_new_source_earned_income (CO-2374): that part takes the 100% disregard and the rest the 67% (phase-10 sweep, OQ-350). Vocabulary fix round (R-1): earned income is cw_gross_earned_income (CO-1716): gross wages plus the self-employment net profit 3.605.2.E.1.c treats as earned income; it had read wages only.

Type money, scope person-month, program ColoradoWorks.
Uses: `cw_earned_income_disregard_rate`, `cw_gross_earned_income`, `cw_in_first_certification_period`, `cw_is_new_earned_income_source`, `cw_new_earnings_disregard_rate`, `cw_new_source_earned_income`, `receives_tanf_cash`.

```
the greater of 0 and Colorado Works: gross earned income minus (if Colorado Works: gross earned income is at most 0;   then 0; else if it is not the case that Receives TANF cash assistance;   then Colorado Works: gross earned income times Colorado Works earned income disregard rate, first certification period and new sources (1); else if Colorado Works first certification period;   then Colorado Works: gross earned income times Colorado Works earned income disregard rate, first certification period and new sources (1); else if it is not the case that Colorado Works: earned income from a new source is unknown;   then (Colorado Works: earned income from a new source times Colorado Works earned income disregard rate, first certification period and new sources (1)) plus ((Colorado Works: gross earned income minus Colorado Works: earned income from a new source) times Colorado Works earned income disregard rate (payment computation) (0.67)); else if Colorado Works new source of earned income;   then Colorado Works: gross earned income times Colorado Works earned income disregard rate, first certification period and new sources (1); otherwise Colorado Works: gross earned income times Colorado Works earned income disregard rate (payment computation) (0.67))
```

### CO-946 Adult Financial: countable income `@engine`

The person's total countable income for the month for Adult Financial purposes, per 9 CCR 2503-5 3.533 (OAP), 3.544 (AND-SO) and 3.549 (AND-CS) - countable unearned income is gross unearned income less any SSI, less the $20 disregard (never below zero, so an SSI-only client gets none), with the full SSI added back (A.2.a-e); for OAP and AND-CS clients, unearned income includes the in-kind support and maintenance the county determines, up to the ISM maximum (3.520.79); when gross unearned income is under $20 the unused part of the $20 goes to the earned income calculation (A.2.f); countable earned income is gross earned income less that unused amount and $65, divided by two (A.1).

Precision. SSI is read as ssi_income (CO-849) when receives_ssi is true and as zero otherwise, so a non-SSI client needs no ssi_income statement. 'Gross unearned income' in A.2.f is read literally as A.2.a's 'gross unearned income from all sources', SSI included, so an SSI recipient whose other unearned income is under $20 has no unused disregard to roll to earnings (OQ-351); the unused amount is subtracted before the $65, the SSI order of 20 CFR 416.1112(c). The ISM term is limited to an OAP-age person or an AND-CS-eligible person (af_is_oap_age, af_and_cs_eligible, neither of which reads this item) because 3.520.79 applies to OAP and AND-CS only. See OQ-114 - does not add a deemed amount from a non-recipient spouse or a sponsor, and does not split the $20 between married clients (A.2.c.1). Reuses ssi_earned_income_exclusion (CO-231, $65), ssi_earned_income_disregard_rate (CO-232, one-half), and ssi_general_income_exclusion (CO-230, $20) cross-program, because 3.533/3.544/3.549's disregard amounts are the identical dollar figures the SSI-related Medicaid chapter's own $65 and $20 disregards carry (20 CFR 416.1112(c), 416.1124(c)(12)), so an Adult-Financial-prefixed duplicate parameter of the same value is not created. Vocabulary fix round (R-1): gross earned income includes the self-employment net profit of 3.520.783.B (af_self_employment_net_profit, CO-1708); unearned income no longer includes the Adult Financial grant itself (the shared cash assistance fact was split, and tanf_cash_income is Colorado Works only).

Type money, scope person-month, program AdultFinancial.
Uses: `af_and_cs_eligible`, `af_deemed_relative_income`, `af_deemed_sponsor_income`, `af_excluded_earned_income`, `af_excluded_unearned_income`, `af_in_kind_support_and_maintenance`, `af_is_oap_age`, `af_ism_maximum`, `af_self_employment_net_profit`, `child_support_received`, `other_unearned_income_nontaxable`, `other_unearned_income_taxable`, `pension_income`, `receives_ssi`, `social_security_income`, `ssi_earned_income_disregard_rate`, `ssi_earned_income_exclusion`, `ssi_general_income_exclusion`, `ssi_income`, `tanf_cash_income`, `tax_exempt_interest`, `unemployment_income`, `wages_gross`.

### CO-951 Adult Financial: OAP grant amount `@engine`

The monthly Old Age Pension grant payment - for a client resident in a facility listed in 3.532.D for the full calendar month after thirty consecutive days, only a personal needs allowance of at most $79 less countable income (3.532.D, F); otherwise the OAP grant standard minus the client's total countable income, raised to the OAP payment floor by a State Supplementary Payment when it falls below the floor, for a client in the oap category - per 9 CCR 2503-5 3.531.D.2, 3.532.B, D-F and 3.533.

Precision. See OQ-120 - does not model 3.532.B.2's mid-month proration for a client determined eligible on a day other than the first of the month, or 3.532.B.3's same-month program-transition rule. K-2 (phase-8 fix round): the personal needs allowance is read as a grant standard of $79 from which countable income is deducted, with no payment floor (OQ-352); a psychiatric facility stay counts for a client 65 or older (3.532.D.3, af_resides_in_psychiatric_facility_thirty_consecutive_days, CO-2006), and a resident of an unlicensed private or uncertified public facility gets neither a PNA nor a grant (3.532.E.2, af_resides_in_unlicensed_or_uncertified_facility, CO-2007; S1318); inmates are barred through af_meets_residency (CO-942). M-7: Adult Financial grants carry cents (no AF provision states a 'drop the cents' rule, unlike Colorado Works' 3.606.1.K.2, which cw_grant_amount, CO-914, implements by flooring) - deliberate, not an oversight. Phase-10 sweep (OQ-120): in the month containing af_eligibility_date (CO-2391) the grant is prorated by the days from that date through the end of the month over the days in the month (3.532.B.2, 3.543.B.2, 3.548.B.2; the day of eligibility is counted, OQ-491); a client eligible on the first, or with no date stated, gets the full grant. No rounding is stated.

### CO-952 Adult Financial: AND grant amount `@engine`

The monthly Aid to the Needy Disabled (or Aid to the Blind) grant payment - for an AND-SO or AND-CS client resident in a facility listed in 3.543.D or 3.548.D for the full calendar month after thirty consecutive days, only a personal needs allowance of at most $79 less countable income (3.543.D-F, 3.548.D-F); otherwise the applicable AND-SO, AND-CS, or AND-SO-standard (for "ab", per OQ-112) grant standard minus the client's total countable income, floored at zero for AND-SO and AB and raised to the AND-CS payment floor for AND-CS (3.546.C.2, E) - per 9 CCR 2503-5 3.543.B, 3.544, 3.546, 3.548.B, and 3.549.

Precision. See OQ-120 - does not model the equivalent mid-month proration rules 3.543.D.2 and 3.548.B.2 state. K-2 (phase-8 fix round): the personal needs allowance is read as a grant standard of $79 from which countable income is deducted, with no payment floor; a resident of an unlicensed private or uncertified public facility gets neither a PNA nor a grant (3.543.E.2, 3.548.E.2, af_resides_in_unlicensed_or_uncertified_facility, CO-2007; S1318); 3.548.F's rule that an AND-CS grant is not reduced until the month after the first full calendar month in the facility is carried by the supplied fact's full-month meaning, not separately (OQ-352). The Aid to the Blind branch rests on C.R.S. 26-2-111(5) alone: the current rule has no Aid to the Blind program (3.500, S1017; OQ-112 resolved), so no PNA rule reaches it. M-7: Adult Financial grants carry cents (no AF provision states a 'drop the cents' rule, unlike Colorado Works' 3.606.1.K.2, which cw_grant_amount, CO-914, implements by flooring) - deliberate, not an oversight. Phase-10 sweep (OQ-120): in the month containing af_eligibility_date (CO-2391) the grant is prorated by the days from that date through the end of the month over the days in the month (3.532.B.2, 3.543.B.2, 3.548.B.2; the day of eligibility is counted, OQ-491); a client eligible on the first, or with no date stated, gets the full grant. No rounding is stated.

### CO-953 Adult Financial: category `@engine`

The single Adult Financial category this person qualifies under for the month - none for a person receiving or eligible for Colorado Works or closed out of it by a sanction (3.520.61.F, 3.520.71.F); otherwise OAP, AND-CS, AND-SO, Aid to the Blind (statute only), or none - tested in that order, per C.R.S. 26-2-111 and 9 CCR 2503-5 3.520, 3.530-3.534, 3.540-3.544, and 3.546-3.549.

Precision. Phase-8 fix round: K-3 - the Colorado Works bar (af_barred_by_colorado_works, CO-1511) is the last conjunct of every branch (the and_so branch through af_and_so_eligible, CO-1203), since 3.520.61.F makes it a non-financial requirement of every Adult Financial program (OQ-117 resolved); placed last so that a person who fails an earlier test (age, SSI, disability) is not asked the Colorado Works facts. OQ-112 resolved - the current rule has no Aid to the Blind program (3.500, S1017) and a blind client 0-59 is AND-SO (3.520.61.A); the ab branch is kept only as the statute-only route of C.R.S. 26-2-111(5) for a blind person AND-SO does not reach (for example a blind SSDI recipient). OAP (age 60+) and the AND programs (age 0-59) are mutually exclusive by age (3.520.61.A), so the test order among them does not change the result for any one person; AND-CS is tested before AND-SO and AB because an SSI recipient (AND-CS) would otherwise also satisfy AND-SO's or AB's own disability/blindness prongs. Each branch applies its own income (af_countable_income vs. the relevant grant standard), citizenship, and resource (af_meets_resource_limit) test directly, per 3.520.71.A's 'shall' list and 3.533/3.544/3.549's 'equals or exceeds the grant standard, denied' rule, rather than through af_grant_standard (CO-949), which is instead derived from this item's result. The and_so branch also excludes anyone already receiving SSI or SSDI, per 3.540's 'have not been approved for Supplemental Security Income (SSI) or Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI)' - see OQ-138 for the tension with 26-2-111(4)(a)'s SSDI-determined alternative route. Fix round (C-10): the oap branch now reads af_meets_citizenship_requirement_oap (CO-929, no five-year bar) instead of meets_public_assistance_citizenship_requirement (CO-905, renamed from af_meets_citizenship_requirement), because 3.520.61.C and 3.520.68.A both scope the citizenship prong and the bar to AND only; the and_cs/and_so/ab branches keep reading the AND version. Fix round (C-9): the ab branch keeps its `[<=, age, af_and_max_age]` cap - see OQ-112's extended body for why the fetched text (3.520.61.A, S530) does not support dropping it, contrary to the review's proposed fix. See OQ-113, OQ-114, OQ-119, OQ-138, OQ-151, OQ-357 for this item's dependencies' assumptions and unmodeled nuances.

### CO-1289 CCCAP: parent fee by formula `@engine`

The monthly CCCAP parent fee the formula assesses before reductions and exceptions - one percent of gross countable household income at or below 100% of the federal poverty guideline; above it, one percent of income plus fourteen percent of every dollar above the guideline plus $15 for each child in care after the first - per 8 CCR 1403-1 3.124.A and P.

Precision. Through July 2028 (3.124.P, S785): 1% of income at or below the monthly 100% FPG, and above it 1% of income plus 14% of each dollar above the FPG plus $15 for each child in care after the first. The children in care are the household's eligible children: cccap_is_eligible_child requires that care be requested because the child needs care for part of the day (cccap_child_needs_care_for_part_of_day, 3.111.F), so a child not in care is not counted (OQ-254 part 1, resolved). From August 2028 (3.124.Q, S786): marginal rates of 1% up to 100% of the FPG, 3% from 100% to 130%, 5% from 130% to 160% and 7% above 160%, with no per-child amount; Q's bands are written "101%-130", "131%-160%" and "161% and above", read here as continuous at 100%, 130% and 160% so no dollar falls between bands (the band-edge reading stays open, OQ-254). The guideline is the monthly 100% FPG of 3.111.H.2-3 (cccap_poverty_guideline_monthly_table) in force on the month's date.

### CO-1290 CCCAP: parent fee `@engine`

The monthly parent fee (co-payment) an eligible CCCAP household pays its child care provider - the formula amount, reduced by 20% when a top-three quality-rated provider is used and to 55% when all children are in part-time care, in whole dollars with the cents dropped - or nothing for a household with no income, a protective services household, a Colorado Works household whose caretakers have no paid employment, or a household that is not eligible, per 8 CCR 1403-1 3.124.A, H, I, P and U.

Precision. The county-discretion waivers (dual Head Start enrollment, teen-parent hardship, disaster, the $5 hardship reduction; 3.124.G, I.1, I.8, S, X) and the homelessness stabilization period (I.5) are not modeled; a protective services household's fee where a child has countable income (I.6) is read as zero because the volume does not separate child income for that program (OQ-254). A Colorado Works household is read as having no paid employment when no household member has earned or self-employment income.

Type money, scope person-month, program CCCAP.
Uses: `all_children_in_part_time_care`, `cccap_eligibility_status`, `cccap_household_income`, `cccap_household_members`, `cccap_parent_fee_formula_amount`, `cccap_self_employment_net_earnings`, `uses_top_quality_rated_provider`, `wages_gross`.

```
if it is not the case that CCCAP: eligibility status is one of: eligible_low_income, eligible_colorado_works, eligible_protective_services
  then 0
else if CCCAP: household income is at most 0
  then 0
else if CCCAP: eligibility status is equal to eligible_protective_services
  then 0
else if all of the following are true:
    - CCCAP: eligibility status is equal to eligible_colorado_works
    - (the sum of that person's Gross wages plus that person's CCCAP: countable self-employment income for each person in CCCAP: household members) is equal to 0
  then 0
otherwise 0 minus (0 minus (CCCAP: parent fee by formula times ((if Uses a top-three quality-rated child care provider;   then 0.8; otherwise 1) times (if All children in part-time care;   then 0.55; otherwise 1))) rounded up to the next whole dollar)
```
