### CO-981 CCCAP: is a teen parent `@engine`

The person is a "teen parent" under 8 CCR 1403-1 3.103.EEEEE (version effective 2026-08-14) - a person under twenty-one years of age who is financially contributing to the welfare of the child, is the parent, adoptive parent, stepparent, legal guardian or person acting in loco parentis with custody of the child for the period care is requested, and is in an eligible activity such as attending basic education, employment, self-employment, or job search. A person under twenty-one who participates in workforce training or post-secondary education is an adult caretaker, not a teen parent.

Precision. Phase-8 fix round (K-7): the current definition (S1016) adds the financially-contributing conjunct, read from is_financially_contributing_to_child (CO-897) with no default (OQ-135, resolved), and moves a person in workforce training or post-secondary education (is_in_workforce_training_or_post_secondary_education, CO-1518, no default) to adult caretaker. Custody is read from a stated parent/child or caretaker/dependent relationship to a CCCAP-eligible child, the same convention cw_has_dependent_child (CO-902) uses for Colorado Works. Requires the custodial child to be a cccap_is_eligible_child, which 3.103.ZZZZ's own text ('his/her child(ren)') does not state; this narrows the term slightly, but costs nothing in practice, since a teen parent with no eligible child also has no eligible child in the household under 3.103.GGG. The eligible-activity conjunct is read with [otherwise, ..., false] (defaults to not-in-an-activity when the case does not state hours_worked/is_in_job_search_activity/snap_is_enrolled_half_time_in_school_or_training for this person), for the same case-coverage reason as OQ-134/OQ-135/OQ-136 - most existing cases in this chapter's own item tests do not state activity facts for a custodial minor whose teen-parent status was previously age-and-custody-only - see OQ-157. Phase-10 sweep: the referral, financially-contributing and activity facts are read without a default; a case states them (OQ-134, OQ-135, OQ-157, OQ-395).

### CO-985 CCCAP: household income `@engine`

The CCCAP household's total countable gross income for the month under 8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.I - every member's unearned income, plus every member's earned income except that of a household child (3.103.GGG) who is not a teen parent, since 3.111.J.1 excludes only "earnings of a child in the household when not a teen parent," not a household child's unearned income or a non-household-child's earnings.

Precision. Sums social_security_income, pension_income, unemployment_income, child_support_received, and other_unearned_income_nontaxable over every cccap_household_member, and adds wages_gross plus self_employment_net_earnings_for_tax for each member except a cccap_is_household_child (CO-990) who is not a cccap_is_teen_parent (CO-981); 3.111.J.1's exclusion is keyed to the 3.103.GGG household-child term, not the narrower 3.111.F eligible-child term, so an eligible child (under 3.111.F) who is not also a household child keeps no special treatment here, and a household child's own unearned income (for example survivor's Social Security under 3.111.I.25) is counted. Does not apply the child-support-paid adjustment of 3.111.K (out of scope this batch; see OQ-162's sibling gap and 3.111.K's own precision note below). Vocabulary fix round (R-1): the supplied income facts are gross amounts received; self-employment is CCCAP's own 3.111.I.2 figure (cccap_self_employment_net_earnings, CO-1710). The 3.111.J exclusions (SSI, SNAP/WIC/school meals, foster/kinship/adoption subsidy payments, LEAP benefits, the Earned Income Credit, student grants and loans, irregular income under $90 a quarter) are not modeled: a case that has such income leaves it out of the supplied amounts (OQ-162). J.26 (public cash assistance) is correct by construction since this item does not read tanf_cash_income or adult_financial_cash_income.

Uses: `cccap_excluded_income`, `cccap_household_members`, `cccap_is_household_child`, `cccap_is_teen_parent`, `cccap_self_employment_net_earnings`, `child_support_received`, `other_unearned_income_nontaxable`, `other_unearned_income_taxable`, `pension_income`, `social_security_income`, `tax_exempt_interest`, `unemployment_income`, `wages_gross`.

### CO-989 CCCAP: eligibility status `@engine`

This CCCAP household's eligibility determination for the month, reported on every household member (including a child, who reads the household's caretakers' and other members' facts rather than their own) - checked in order - a Protective Services referral within its own household-of-one income test, Colorado Works Child Care eligibility, having an eligible child in the household, being in an eligible activity, the county entry income limit, and, last, the remaining Low-Income criteria (residency, the asset self-declaration) bundled in cccap_low_income_child_care_eligible - eligible for Low-Income Child Care only if every one of those checks passes.

Precision. Colorado Works Child Care households are not subject to the low-income eligible-activity or entry-income tests (3.111.D.6), so that route is checked first and short-circuits the rest. Protective Services households are not subject to the low-income eligible-activity or residency-verification requirements (3.119.D, E), but 3.119.A does not waive the income test - it only redefines it (household of one, placed child's income only, no child support) - so the Protective Services branch now carries its own income conjunct (cccap_protective_services_income_within_limit, CO-995) and falls through to the ordinary rows, rather than granting eligible_protective_services on the referral flag alone. A residency or asset-limit failure that survives to the final row (the only two 3.111 criteria this item does not give their own reason code) reports the generic ineligible rather than a more specific option, since the outcome's option list has no ineligible_residency or ineligible_assets entry.

Type one of, scope person-month, program CCCAP.
Uses: `cccap_colorado_works_child_care_eligible`, `cccap_household_caretakers_in_eligible_activity`, `cccap_household_members`, `cccap_is_eligible_child`, `cccap_low_income_child_care_eligible`, `cccap_meets_income_guidelines`, `cccap_protective_services_income_within_limit`, `is_protective_services_child_care_case`.

```
if all of the following are true:
    - Open Protective Services child care referral
    - CCCAP: protective services income within the size-1 limit
  then eligible_protective_services
else if CCCAP: Colorado Works child care eligible
  then eligible_colorado_works
else if it is not the case that (there is a person in CCCAP: household members such that;   that person's CCCAP: is an eligible child)
  then ineligible_child
else if it is not the case that CCCAP: household caretakers in eligible activity
  then ineligible_activity
else if it is not the case that CCCAP: meets the income eligibility guidelines
  then ineligible_income
else if it is not the case that CCCAP: low-income child care eligible
  then ineligible
otherwise eligible_low_income
```

### CO-1000 LEAP: household members `@engine`

The individuals living together as one economic unit for whom primary heating fuel is customarily purchased in common, or who make undesignated payments for heat in the form of rent, under 9 CCR 2503-7 3.751.1's "Household" definition - a spouse, or a child under eighteen living in the same dwelling as the parent or guardian (unless emancipated), per 3.751.2.D, or anyone the case states shares heating fuel in common under 3.751.1's general economic-unit test, reciprocally closed - leaving out a person who does not live at the dwelling (institutional group care), a member already counted in another household approved for the same eligibility period (3.751.2.A), a member who does not meet the citizenship requirement (3.753.18), and a member who meets it as declared but has provided no SSN or proof of application for one (3.751.1 "Completed Application" B) or whose declared immigration status SAVE has not verified (3.753.15, 3.753.17.A). The income of a member left out for status or verification is still counted (leap_household_members_for_income, CO-1009).

Precision. As with snap_household_members (CO-305), a stated spouse or parent/child relationship edge is read as living together for LEAP purposes, extended beyond 3.751.2.D's unconditional age-based joins by the supplied shares_heating_fuel_with (CO-895), and by a stated shares_heat_with relationship, which joins any two persons who buy heating fuel in common, related or not (OQ-132, resolved), except that an edge is not crossed to or from a person whose own leap_living_arrangement is institutional_group_care: 3.751.1 joins individuals "living together" and 3.751.2.B counts "each person living at a dwelling", so a spouse who has entered a nursing facility is not in the household at home (OQ-358, resolved). If leap_living_arrangement is not stated, LEAP reads it as an ordinary dwelling. The SSN test reads ssn_is_verified (a number furnished, an application shown, or SSA's confirmation); 3.751.1 B states no exception for a person who cannot obtain a number. This volume does not separately model 3.751.2.E's separate-household election for a parent living with an ex-spouse after divorce or legal separation, or 3.751.21's permanent-separation test.

### CO-1281 LEAP: Heating Fuel Assistance benefit amount `@engine`

The heating-season Heating Fuel Assistance benefit for an eligible household - one amount for the whole November-April season, reported on each month of the season in which the household is eligible, not a monthly payment to be multiplied by the months - the adjusted estimated home heating costs less the statewide adjustment and the household income contribution (each a share of those costs), less the subsidized-housing heating allowance where it applies, kept within the Department's minimum and maximum for the program year - or zero when the household is not eligible, per 9 CCR 2503-7 3.758.47 Steps B, D, F and G.

Precision. Step G subtracts the Step B-F adjustments from the estimated costs; this item reads Steps B and D as shares of the costs after Steps C and E and subtracts them together, then deducts the $180 seasonal subsidized-housing allowance (Step F), and floors the result at zero before the minimum and maximum apply. ### CO-1292 Is school aged `@engine`

Whether the child is of Colorado's compulsory school attendance age for the school year that began on the most recent August 1: the child had attained the age of six on or before that August 1 and was under seventeen on it (C.R.S. 22-33-104(1)(a)). 7 CFR 292.2 makes these the "school aged" years for Summer EBT.

Precision. The August 1 is the most recent one on or before the determination date, computed from a fixed August anchor (2000-08-01) advanced by whole years, as leap_program_year_start_month (CO-1006) does for November; the pattern catalog reads no month-of-year number out of a date. A determination dated in June or July (inside the summer operational period) therefore reads the school year just ended, and one dated from August 1 reads the school year just begun. The exceptions of 22-33-104(2) excuse individual children from attendance (illness, private or home schooling, graduation) and do not change the ages; 292.6 reaches a child who is school aged "at any time during the period of eligibility", and the item tests the one August 1 named above.

```
  - (the number of whole years between Date of birth and the first day of (the number of whole years between 2000-08-01 and the Determination Date) times 12 months after 2000-08) is at least Compulsory school attendance minimum age (6)
  - (the number of whole years between Date of birth and the first day of (the number of whole years between 2000-08-01 and the Determination Date) times 12 months after 2000-08) is less than Compulsory school attendance age limit (17)
```

### CO-1298 Summer EBT (SUN Bucks): eligibility status `@engine`

Whether the child is eligible for Summer EBT (Colorado's SUN Bucks) and on which ground - categorically eligible (a member of a household receiving SNAP or TANF, or another categorical ground) and either school aged or enrolled in an NSLP/SBP school; or enrolled in an NSLP/SBP school with household income at or below the reduced-price meal guideline - per 7 CFR 292.2, 292.5 and 292.6.

Precision. SNAP receipt is read as the child's own SNAP eligibility in the month (snap_is_eligible), TANF receipt as receives_tanf_cash. A child for whom any categorical prong is unknown and the income test is not met is unknown. The period of eligibility spans the preceding school year through the summer (292.7); this item tests the facts of the month evaluated. School age is derived from Colorado's compulsory attendance ages (is_school_aged, CO-1292, C.R.S. 22-33-104(1)(a)). Colorado's choices among the optional streamlined-certification sources (Medicaid and other means-tested programs, 292.12(d)(2)) are not in any published Colorado text: there is no Colorado Summer EBT rule (OQ-255).

Type one of, scope person-month, program SunBucks.
Uses: `is_enrolled_in_nslp_school`, `is_school_aged`, `receives_tanf_cash`, `school_meal_household_income`, `sebt_income_eligibility_limit`, `sebt_other_categorical_basis`, `snap_is_eligible`.

```
if all of the following are true:
    - any of the following is true:
      - Is school aged
      - Enrolled in an NSLP or SBP school
    - any of the following is true:
      - SNAP: is eligible
      - Receives TANF cash assistance
      - Other Summer EBT categorical basis
  then eligible_categorical
else if all of the following are true:
    - Enrolled in an NSLP or SBP school
    - School meal household monthly income is at most Summer EBT: monthly income eligibility limit
  then eligible_income
otherwise ineligible
```

```json
["case",[["all",["any","is_school_aged","is_enrolled_in_nslp_school"],["any","snap_is_eligible","receives_tanf_cash","sebt_other_categorical_basis"]],"eligible_categorical"],[["all","is_enrolled_in_nslp_school",["<=","school_meal_household_income","sebt_income_eligibility_limit"]],"eligible_income"],["else","ineligible"]]
```

Examples: 4, all passing.

### CO-1299 Summer EBT (SUN Bucks): summer benefit amount `@engine`

The total Summer EBT benefit for an eligible child - the monthly benefit level for the calendar year times the three summer months - or zero for a child who is not eligible, per 7 CFR 292.15(d)-(e) and the 2026 benefit levels notice ($40 a month, $120 a summer in the 48 States and the District of Columbia).

Precision. The benefit is issued in full for the summer regardless of the date of application (292.15(f)(2)(iii)); the summer operational period is the agency's and is not modeled.

Type money, scope person-month, program SunBucks.
Uses: `sebt_eligibility_status`, `sebt_monthly_benefit`.

```
if Summer EBT (SUN Bucks): eligibility status is one of: eligible_categorical, eligible_income
  then Summer EBT monthly benefit level (48 States and DC) (40) times 3
otherwise 0
```

```json
["case",[["in","sebt_eligibility_status",["eligible_categorical","eligible_income"]],["*","sebt_monthly_benefit",3]],["else",0]]
```

Examples: 2, all passing.

### CO-1698 SUN Bucks: verification status `@engine`

Where the child's Summer EBT verification stands: not applicable (not school-aged and not in an NSLP or SBP school); no verification required (streamlined certification, or an application not selected); complete; or pending, in which case benefits are not issued until it is complete.

Precision. 292.14 sets no fixed period: the household answers by the date the agency sets, after at least two follow-up attempts, and verification for cause is completed within 30 days of receipt; so there is no past-due state (OQ-377).

Type one of, scope person-month, program SunBucks.
Uses: `is_enrolled_in_nslp_school`, `is_school_aged`, `sebt_pending_verification_count`, `sebt_requires_verification_of_income`, `sebt_requires_verification_of_school_enrollment`.

```
if it is not the case that (any of the following is true:;   - Is school aged;   - Enrolled in an NSLP or SBP school)
  then not_applicable
else if all of the following are true:
    - it is not the case that SUN Bucks: requires verification of income
    - it is not the case that SUN Bucks: requires verification of school enrollment
  then not_required
else if SUN Bucks: pending verification count is equal to 0
  then complete
otherwise pending
```

```json
["case",[["not",["any","is_school_aged","is_enrolled_in_nslp_school"]],"not_applicable"],[["all",["not","sebt_requires_verification_of_income"],["not","sebt_requires_verification_of_school_enrollment"]],"not_required"],[["=","sebt_pending_verification_count",0],"complete"],["else","pending"]]
```

Examples: 4, all passing.

### CO-1699 SUN Bucks: requires verification of income `@engine`

Whether the child's household must verify income for Summer EBT: an application selected for verification (sample or for cause), unless the child is categorically eligible through SNAP, TANF or another approved program, or is homeless.

Precision. 292.14(f)(1) excepts a household whose children are all determined eligible from SNAP, FDPIR, TANF or another approved means-tested program's documentation, or are all foster, homeless, migrant or runaway children. SNAP and TANF are read from snap_is_eligible and receives_tanf_cash; FDPIR, another approved program and the foster, migrant and runaway grounds are within sebt_other_categorical_basis (CO-1296), and homelessness is is_homeless. sebt_other_categorical_basis also carries Head Start and individual free or reduced-price certification, which (f)(1) does not list, so such a child is excepted here too; and the item tests the child, not every child in the household (OQ-377).

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program SunBucks.
Uses: `is_homeless`, `receives_tanf_cash`, `sebt_application_is_selected_for_verification`, `sebt_other_categorical_basis`, `snap_is_eligible`.

```
all of the following are true:
  - Summer EBT application selected for verification
  - it is not the case that (any of the following is true:;   - any of the following is true:;     - SNAP: is eligible;     - Receives TANF cash assistance;     - Other Summer EBT categorical basis;   - Is homeless)
```

```json
["all","sebt_application_is_selected_for_verification",["not",["any",["any","snap_is_eligible","receives_tanf_cash","sebt_other_categorical_basis"],"is_homeless"]]]
```

Examples: 3, all passing.
